title: LEGO: Leveled Language Gaussian Splatting
comment: Accepted to ECCV 2026. Project page: https://pz0826.github.io/LEGO-Webpage/
summary: We introduce LEGO for advanced open-vocabulary scene understanding. Beyond basic concept recognition, its core innovation lies in capturing the intrinsic semantic hierarchies within the scene, such as the "flowerpot -> bouquet -> bud -> petal" lineage. While foundation models like SAM can identify multi-granular structures in 2D, their partitions are strictly perspective-bound and lack cross-view consensus. LEGO self-adaptively re-grades volatile multi-view SAM granularities into a unified, 3D-consistent hierarchy. This provides precise supervision for the structurally coherent, multi-level segmentation of 3D scenes. By grounding these segments with CLIP embeddings, LEGO recovers open-vocabulary semantic logic across hierarchical levels. Furthermore, by incorporating spatial relationships, we elevate these segments into level-wise language scene graphs, effectively empowering Large Language Models to perform complex, context-aware spatial reasoning and precise visual grounding. Experimental results demonstrate that LEGO establishes new state-of-the-art performance across both promptable and open-vocabulary 3D segmentation benchmarks, exhibiting advanced hierarchical scene decomposition and context-aware spatial reasoning.

AI.tldr: LEGO is a method for open-vocabulary 3D scene understanding that captures intrinsic semantic hierarchies (e.g., flowerpot → bouquet → bud → petal) by re-grading multi-view SAM granularities into a unified 3D-consistent hierarchy, grounding segments with CLIP embeddings, and constructing level-wise language scene graphs to enable LLM-driven spatial reasoning and visual grounding.
AI.motivation: Foundation models like SAM can identify multi-granular structures in 2D, but their partitions are perspective-bound and lack cross-view consensus, making it difficult to achieve structurally coherent, multi-level semantic segmentation in 3D scenes. Existing methods focus only on basic concept recognition rather than intrinsic hierarchical understanding.
AI.method: LEGO self-adaptively re-grades volatile multi-view SAM granularities into a unified, 3D-consistent hierarchy, providing supervision for structurally coherent multi-level 3D segmentation. Segments are grounded with CLIP embeddings to recover open-vocabulary semantics, and spatial relationships are incorporated to build level-wise language scene graphs that empower LLMs for complex reasoning.
AI.result: LEGO achieves state-of-the-art performance on both promptable and open-vocabulary 3D segmentation benchmarks, demonstrating advanced hierarchical scene decomposition and context-aware spatial reasoning.
AI.conclusion: Capturing multi-granular semantic hierarchies with 3D consistency, combined with LLM-accessible language scene graphs, is a powerful direction for advanced open-vocabulary 3D scene understanding.

title: Signpost Watermarking: Joint Optimization for Visual Watermark Coexistence
summary: We present a method for training imperceptible visual watermarks to coexist with other such watermarks. Recent work has shown that independently trained image watermarking models can coexist with surprisingly limited interference, enabling watermark ensembling. However, this coexistence is a serendipitous property rather than an explicit optimization objective, leaving interference uncontrolled and potentially reducing decoding robustness or visual quality. We first show empirically that the same coexistence property extends to video watermarking. We then show that both image and video watermarks can be trained with a decoder-aware objective to improve coexistence. Our results suggest a practical path to signpost watermarks that indicate the presence of independently deployed provenance watermarking systems, supporting layered provenance signaling for content authenticity and rights.

AI.tldr: A method to train imperceptible visual watermarks that deliberately coexist with other watermarks via a decoder-aware objective, improving layered provenance signaling for content authenticity.
AI.motivation: Existing watermark ensembling works by serendipity rather than design, leaving interference uncontrolled which can harm decoding robustness and visual quality. The authors aim to make coexistence an explicit optimization objective.
AI.method: First empirically demonstrates that coexistence properties extend from image to video watermarking, then trains both image and video watermarks with a decoder-aware objective that explicitly optimizes for coexistence with independently deployed watermarking systems.
AI.result: Shows that decoder-aware training improves coexistence for both image and video watermarks, enabling more reliable layered watermark signaling.
AI.conclusion: The approach provides a practical path to layered provenance signaling, where signpost watermarks indicate the presence of independently deployed provenance watermarking systems, supporting content authenticity and rights management.

title: 4D-WAM: 4D Consistent World Modeling for Autonomous Driving
summary: Emerging World-Action Models (WAMs) have demonstrated promising performance in autonomous driving by jointly modeling future driving scene evolution and trajectory planning. However, existing WAMs are typically trained with video data, which is only 2D projections of the underlying 4D driving scene. Consequently, WAMs fail to understand and capture the structure of 4D scenes and thus generate visually plausible yet 4D inconsistent future predictions that mislead downstream planning. To alleviate this issue, we present 4D-WAM, a model that leverages geometric foundation models for training-time supervision to enable 4D consistent world modeling. Specifically, we feed WAM-predicted future frames into a geometric foundation model, and use 4D-aware responses to define a 4D consistency loss. This loss encourages the model to understand, represent, and predict physically consistent 4D scenes during training, without additional inference cost. Moreover, we identify an early-decision phenomenon in WAMs and propose a decision-oriented timestep sampling strategy that emphasizes supervision at early, high-noise stages, where driving decisions are primarily formed. By propagating 4D supervision to this critical decision-formation phase, the proposed strategy further improves trajectory planning. Extensive experiments demonstrate that 4D-WAM effectively models 4D consistent scene evolution and achieves state-of-the-art performance on challenging NAVSIM-v1 and NAVSIM-v2 benchmarks.

AI.tldr: 4D-WAM enhances World-Action Models (WAMs) for autonomous driving by using geometric foundation models to provide 4D consistency supervision during training, enabling physically consistent scene prediction and improved trajectory planning without extra inference cost.
AI.motivation: Existing World-Action Models (WAMs) are trained only on 2D video projections of 4D driving scenes, so they fail to capture 4D structure and generate visually plausible but 4D-inconsistent predictions that mislead downstream planning.
AI.method: 4D-WAM feeds WAM-predicted future frames into a geometric foundation model and uses 4D-aware responses to define a 4D consistency loss during training. It also identifies an early-decision phenomenon and proposes a decision-oriented timestep sampling strategy that emphasizes supervision at early, high-noise stages where driving decisions are primarily formed.
AI.result: 4D-WAM effectively models 4D consistent scene evolution and achieves state-of-the-art performance on the NAVSIM-v1 and NAVSIM-v2 benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: By incorporating 4D-aware supervision during training and focusing on the critical decision-formation phase, 4D-WAM enables 4D consistent world modeling that improves trajectory planning, all without additional inference overhead.

title: P3CA: Encoder-Agnostic Interpretation of Vision Foundation Model Embeddings via Spatial Probing
comment: 10 pages, 5 figures, 1 table. Accepted at the iMIMIC Workshop, MICCAI 2026. This arXiv version is the pre-peer-review author manuscript
summary: Vision foundation models are increasingly used as reusable encoders in medical image computing, yet their high-dimensional spatial embeddings are difficult to inspect beyond downstream task performance or global dimensionality reduction. We propose position-prompted PCA (P3CA), an encoder-agnostic method for local probing of channel-rich spatial tensors. Given a user-selected spatial prompt, P3CA estimates the feature normalization and dominant covariance directions within that region, then applies the resulting projection to the full tensor to visualize where locally informative directions are expressed. This produces a region-conditioned representation lens without modifying the encoder, retraining, or requiring task-specific labels. We implement P3CA in EmbedVision, an interactive 3D Slicer-based workflow, and evaluate it across natural images, colorectal pathology foundation-model embeddings, and spatial transcriptomic tensors. Across these settings, prompted projections reveal local structure suppressed by global PCA, improve prompt-matched pathology discrimination from frozen three-dimensional projections, and support comparison between learned and measured spatial representations.

AI.tldr: P3CA is an encoder-agnostic method for local probing of channel-rich spatial tensors using position-prompted PCA, implemented in an interactive 3D Slicer workflow called EmbedVision, showing improvements over global PCA across natural images, pathology foundation models, and spatial transcriptomics.
AI.motivation: Vision foundation models are used as reusable encoders in medical imaging, but their high-dimensional spatial embeddings are hard to inspect beyond downstream task metrics or global dimensionality reduction, limiting interpretability of local structures.
AI.method: P3CA estimates feature normalization and dominant covariance directions within a user-selected spatial prompt region, then applies the resulting projection to the full tensor to visualize where locally informative directions are expressed, without modifying the encoder or requiring labels.
AI.result: Prompted projections reveal local structure suppressed by global PCA, improve prompt-matched pathology discrimination from frozen 3D projections, and support comparison between learned and measured spatial representations across natural images, pathology embeddings, and spatial transcriptomics.
AI.conclusion: P3CA provides a region-conditioned representation lens that enables local interpretability of foundation model embeddings without retraining, useful for medical image analysis and multi-modal spatial data comparison.

title: MAD-HOI: Masked Autoregressive Diffusion for Generating Articulated Hand Object Interactions from Text
summary: Methods for text-based generation of hand-object interaction (HOI) sequences primarily focus on producing smooth, physically plausible trajectories. A truly utilitarian method should additionally support variable-length generation, composite motion sequences, motion completion and infilling, and reliable termination without compromising physical plausibility. Standard diffusion models for HOI generation are typically trained only for text-to-motion generation on atomic motions and require the motion length to be specified a-priori. Autoregressive (AR) methods provide greater sequence-level flexibility, but commonly depend on discrete motion codes, which can lose contact-sensitive motion detail. To address these key limitations, we present a model performing Masked Autoregression with Diffusion for HOI generation (MAD-HOI). Our method starts by encoding hand and object motions in a continuous latent space while keeping them disentangled to maintain stream-wise control. This is followed by a masked autoregressive transformer to predict context features that condition a flow-matching head. MAD-HOI is capable of motion generation for atomic and composite articulated sequences, conditioned motion completion and infilling, as well as EOM (End of Motion) prediction from a single training objective. We provide comprehensive evaluations for these capabilities and benchmark our method on the ARCTIC and GRAB datasets. Our experiments demonstrate that our method generates more diverse and physically plausible interactions compared to other open-sourced baseline methods.

AI.tldr: MAD-HOI combines masked autoregression with diffusion to generate hand-object interaction sequences, enabling variable-length text-to-motion generation, composite sequences, motion completion/infilling, and end-of-motion prediction from a single training objective.
AI.motivation: Existing methods for text-based hand-object interaction generation are limited: diffusion models require pre-specified motion lengths and only handle atomic motions, while autoregressive methods depend on discrete motion codes that lose contact-sensitive detail. A practical method needs variable-length generation, composite sequences, motion completion/infilling, and reliable termination while maintaining physical plausibility.
AI.method: MAD-HOI encodes hand and object motions in a disentangled continuous latent space, then uses a masked autoregressive transformer to predict context features that condition a flow-matching head. This single architecture supports atomic and composite motion generation, motion completion and infilling, and End of Motion (EOM) prediction.
AI.result: Comprehensive evaluations on ARCTIC and GRAB datasets show MAD-HOI generates more diverse and physically plausible hand-object interactions compared to other open-sourced baseline methods.
AI.conclusion: MAD-HOI demonstrates that masked autoregression with diffusion can jointly address sequence-level flexibility and high-fidelity motion generation for HOI, providing a unified framework for multiple generation tasks from a single training objective.

title: Motion Artifact-Aware Self-Supervised Representation Learning for 3D Brain MRI Motion Artifact Reduction
summary: Patient motion remains a source of image degradation in brain MRI, leading to signal loss, blurring, and geometric distortion that compromise quantitative analysis. Existing deep learning methods for motion correction typically rely on paired clean-corrupted data or k-space acquisitions, which are rarely available in clinical settings. We propose SSRL-MAR, a motion artifact-aware unpaired representation learning framework for motion artifact reduction that requires neither paired training data nor explicit motion labels. SSRL-MAR employed a three-stage training strategy: (1) contrastive learning on 3D patches to extract motion representations by contrasting clean and synthetically corrupted images, (2) a motion artifact-aware synthesis network to generate motion artifacts from clean scans, and (3) a motion artifact-aware generator to restore clean volumes using the learned degrader for self-supervised supervision. On in-silico dataset, SSRL-MAR achieved PSNR 23.81dB, SSIM 91.55%, and NMSE 0.79%. On in-vivo MR-ART dataset, the pretrained model reduced motion distortion, and unsupervised domain adaptation further improved anatomical fidelity. Against a source-only supervised model trained on the same simulated pairs, SSRL-MAR improved PSNR by up to 2.0 dB on MR-ART after unsupervised domain adaptation, and remained within 0.25-0.47 dB of an oracle supervised model that requires real paired data unavailable in practice. At the milder motion level, volumetric error in structures such as the corpus callosum and ventricular system decreased by more than 50%, confirming improved neuroanatomical consistency. These results indicate that SSRL-MAR provides a robust and scalable image-domain solution for 3D brain MRI motion correction, enabling reliable structural quantification in large-scale neuroimaging studies without requiring prospectively acquired pairs or acquisition-specific calibration.

AI.tldr: SSRL-MAR is an unpaired representation learning framework for 3D brain MRI motion artifact reduction that requires no paired training data or motion labels. Using a three-stage approach (contrastive learning, motion-aware synthesis, and self-supervised restoration), it achieves strong performance on in-silico data (PSNR 23.81dB, SSIM 91.55%) and improves over source-only supervised models by up to 2.0 dB on in-vivo MR-ART data after unsupervised domain adaptation, coming within 0.25-0.47 dB of an oracle supervised model.
AI.motivation: Patient motion degrades brain MRI quality, causing signal loss, blurring, and geometric distortion that compromise quantitative analysis. Existing deep learning motion correction methods require paired clean-corrupted data or k-space acquisitions, which are rarely available in clinical practice, motivating the need for a method that works without paired training data or explicit motion labels.
AI.method: SSRL-MAR employs a three-stage training strategy: (1) contrastive learning on 3D patches to extract motion representations by contrasting clean and synthetically corrupted images, (2) a motion artifact-aware synthesis network that generates motion artifacts from clean scans, and (3) a motion artifact-aware generator that restores clean volumes using the learned degrader for self-supervised supervision.
AI.result: On in-silico dataset: PSNR 23.81dB, SSIM 91.55%, NMSE 0.79%. On in-vivo MR-ART dataset, the pretrained model reduced motion distortion, with unsupervised domain adaptation further improving anatomical fidelity. SSRL-MAR improved PSNR by up to 2.0 dB over source-only supervised model after domain adaptation, and remained within 0.25-0.47 dB of an oracle supervised model. At milder motion levels, volumetric errors in the corpus callosum and ventricular system decreased by more than 50%.
AI.conclusion: SSRL-MAR provides a robust and scalable image-domain solution for 3D brain MRI motion correction, enabling reliable structural quantification in large-scale neuroimaging studies without requiring prospectively acquired pairs or acquisition-specific calibration.

title: DoseBridge: Denoising Diffusion Bridge Model for Dose Prediction in Lung Intensity-Modulated Proton Therapy
summary: Most radiotherapy dose-prediction models use only CT images and anatomical structures, although intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) dose also depends strongly on beam geometry and available clinical datasets are often small. We present DoseBridge, a denoising diffusion bridge model that uses the patient CT as a structured bridge endpoint and encodes plan-specific beam geometry in a spatially aligned beam mask. Multiscale fusion combines CT, target, organ-at-risk, and beam-mask representations with 1.95% additional parameters. DoseBridge was retrospectively evaluated on single-institution CT images and treatment plans from 52 patients with advanced-stage lung cancer treated with 60 Gy in 30 fractions; 42 cases were used for training and 10 for testing. Performance was assessed using image-similarity, dose-volume, and Lyman-Kutcher-Burman normal-tissue complication probability (NTCP) metrics and compared with two deep-learning models. On the test cohort, DoseBridge achieved a mean absolute error of 4.170 Gy, peak signal-to-noise ratio of 23.06 dB, and structural similarity index of 0.798, outperforming both comparison models on these metrics. Clinical target volume D95 differed from the reference dose by 0.62 +/- 1.6 Gy; signed organ-at-risk mean-dose differences ranged from -0.32 to 0.24 Gy, and NTCP differences were -0.40 +/- 2.2 and 0.52 +/- 3.4 percentage points for acute esophagitis and radiation pneumonitis, respectively. Changing only the beam mask redirected predicted low-dose entrance regions while preserving the high-dose target region. To our knowledge, DoseBridge is the first denoising diffusion bridge model for radiotherapy dose prediction. These results support its feasibility as a beam-aware planning prior for lung IMPT, pending evaluation in larger external cohorts.

AI.tldr: DoseBridge is the first denoising diffusion bridge model for radiotherapy dose prediction, using patient CT as a bridge endpoint and plan-specific beam geometry in a spatially aligned beam mask, with only 1.95% additional parameters through multiscale fusion. Evaluated on 52 lung cancer patients (42 training, 10 testing), it outperformed two deep-learning baselines on image-similarity metrics (MAE 4.170 Gy, PSNR 23.06 dB, SSIM 0.798), showed clinically acceptable dose-volume and NTCP differences, and demonstrated beam-awareness by redirecting low-dose entrance regions when the beam mask was changed.
AI.motivation: Most radiotherapy dose-prediction models rely only on CT images and anatomical structures, but intensity-modulated proton therapy (IMPT) dose distribution depends strongly on beam geometry as well. Additionally, clinical datasets for such tasks are often small, creating a need for a model that can incorporate beam geometry information without requiring large amounts of training data.
AI.method: DoseBridge is a denoising diffusion bridge model that uses the patient CT as a structured bridge endpoint and encodes plan-specific beam geometry via a spatially aligned beam mask. A multiscale fusion mechanism integrates CT, target, organ-at-risk, and beam-mask representations with only 1.95% additional parameters over the base model.
AI.result: In a retrospective evaluation on 52 lung cancer patients (60 Gy/30 fractions), DoseBridge outperformed two deep-learning comparison models with a mean absolute error of 4.170 Gy, PSNR of 23.06 dB, and SSIM of 0.798. Clinical target volume D95 differed by 0.62±1.6 Gy; organ-at-risk mean-dose differences ranged from -0.32 to 0.24 Gy; NTCP differences were -0.40±2.2 and 0.52±3.4 percentage points for acute esophagitis and radiation pneumonitis. Changing only the beam mask redirected low-dose entrance regions while preserving the high-dose target region.
AI.conclusion: DoseBridge demonstrates feasibility as the first beam-aware denoising diffusion bridge model for lung IMPT dose prediction, supporting its potential as a planning prior. However, validation in larger external cohorts is needed before broader clinical adoption.

title: Human versus Computer Vision
summary: Computer vision saliency models predict where people will look, one map per image, and a billion-dollar predicted-attention industry sells those maps in place of measuring real viewers. I test the leading models from the audience side, against 11.4 million webcam gaze points from 3,023 US adults recruited to national quotas, viewing circulating news photographs. I show that an untrained central marker outperforms every trained network, because the content the networks add on top of the center falls where these audiences never look. What accuracy remains is systematically biased, favoring younger, White, and moderate viewers over older, Black, and ideologically extreme ones. I propose a way forward and build on what a group's own gaze reveals about whether a model can learn that group at all, and I apply it across every demographic axis this sample supports. Ultimately, I show how systems that decide what people see can learn to see everyone, and this study supplies the standard by which such a claim should be judged.

AI.tldr: This study evaluates leading computer vision saliency models against 11.4 million webcam gaze points from 3,023 demographically representative US adults viewing news photographs, finding that an untrained central marker outperforms all trained networks. The models' remaining accuracy is systematically biased against older, Black, and ideologically extreme viewers. The paper proposes a method to assess whether a group's gaze can be learned by a model and applies it across demographic axes, ultimately advocating for systems that can learn to see all people.
AI.motivation: The paper challenges the assumption that commercial saliency models accurately predict where real audiences look, given a billion-dollar industry sells these maps in place of measuring actual viewers. The author tests these models from the audience side using large-scale real gaze data to expose their limitations and biases.
AI.method: The author collected 11.4 million webcam gaze points from 3,023 US adults recruited to national quotas, viewing circulating news photographs. Leading saliency models were tested against this data, and also compared against a simple untrained central marker baseline. The paper then proposes a diagnostic method to determine whether a group's gaze patterns are learnable by models, applied across demographic axes.
AI.result: An untrained central marker outperforms every trained network, indicating that model-added content falls where audiences never look. Remaining accuracy is systematically biased, favoring younger, White, and moderate viewers over older, Black, and ideologically extreme ones.
AI.conclusion: Systems that decide what people see can learn to see everyone, and this study provides the standard by which such claims should be judged. The paper offers a way forward for building more inclusive saliency models.

title: More Accurate, Less Human: Gestalt Grouping in Vision Models
comment: 9 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables. Conditionally accepted to VISxVision 2026, a workshop at IEEE VIS 2026. Includes appendix with per-task stimuli, metric derivations, and full per-model results
summary: Human vision organizes what it sees into wholes: same-colored points group into series, similar marks cohere into categories, and shapes complete into recognizable objects. These are the Gestalt operations that visualization design builds on. Whether vision models organize visual content this way has not been systematically tested. We introduce a behavioral battery that scores models against human data from prior perception studies on four grouping tasks: mark-color odd-one-out, color-series counting, silhouette recognition, and object odd-one-out. We apply it to 45 models across five training families: supervised, self-supervised, and contrastive vision-language encoders, open-weight VLMs, and closed foundation models. The battery reveals that agreement with human responses captures aspects of perceptual organization that conventional performance metrics fail to distinguish, with several closed models exhibiting substantially lower alignment than their benchmark accuracy would suggest. Scoring against published perception data therefore gives visualization research a reusable yardstick, requiring no new user study, for auditing whether the models now entering visualization pipelines organize what they see the way their human audience does.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces a behavioral battery that tests whether vision models organize visual content the way humans do, using four Gestalt-based grouping tasks derived from prior perception studies. They evaluate 45 models across five training families and find that human-agreement scores reveal aspects of perceptual organization that conventional performance metrics miss, with several closed models showing lower human alignment than their benchmark accuracy suggests.
AI.motivation: Human vision organizes visual input into wholes through Gestalt principles (grouping, categorization, shape completion), and visualization design builds on these operations. However, whether vision models actually organize visual content the same way humans do has not been systematically tested, which matters because these models are increasingly entering visualization pipelines.
AI.method: The authors construct a behavioral battery scoring models against human data from prior perception studies on four grouping tasks: mark-color odd-one-out, color-series counting, silhouette recognition, and object odd-one-out. They apply it to 45 models across five training families (supervised, self-supervised, contrastive vision-language encoders, open-weight VLMs, and closed foundation models).
AI.result: The battery reveals that agreement with human responses captures aspects of perceptual organization that conventional performance metrics fail to distinguish. Several closed models exhibit substantially lower human alignment than their benchmark accuracy would suggest.
AI.conclusion: Scoring against published perception data provides visualization research with a reusable yardstick that requires no new user study, enabling auditing of whether models entering visualization pipelines organize what they see the way their human audience does.

title: A Convolutional Layer Activation Dimensionality Reduction for Out-of-Distribution and Adversarial Attack Detection Methods
summary: Despite the success of convolutional neural networks in image classification tasks and their general application in multi-modal models, their susceptibility to out-of-distribution and adversarial attack samples raises concerns regarding trustworthiness and safety. Among the approaches to tackle such issues, detection methods that analyze the model's intermediate activations to estimate a confidence score are a promising family that evaluates the decision process, relying on a dimensionality reduction step to enable efficient downstream processing of the high-dimensional activations. However, when considering convolutional layers, the dimensionality reduction methods in the literature either lack a mechanism to control the compression/information-loss trade-off or yield large representations. In this paper, we carefully analyze two state-of-the-art detection methods and their dimensionality reductions for convolutional layers and develop a novel reduction method with a controllable high-compression level. We extend these two state-of-the-art detection methods, enabling the usage of any dimensionality reduction, and evaluate their performance on out-of-distribution and adversarial attack detection. Results show that the detection methods with the proposed dimensionality reduction consistently perform better than, or comparable to, the strongest alternative. Furthermore, the proposed method is shown to reduce computation and memory footprints, given that it has the highest compression among the compared methods.

AI.tldr: The paper addresses the limitations of dimensionality reduction methods used in activation-based detection approaches for out-of-distribution and adversarial samples in CNNs. The authors propose a novel dimensionality reduction method with controllable high compression, extend two state-of-the-art detection methods to use any dimensionality reduction, and demonstrate that their approach performs better or comparably to existing alternatives while reducing computation and memory footprints.
AI.motivation: CNNs are vulnerable to out-of-distribution and adversarial samples, raising trustworthiness concerns. Detection methods analyzing intermediate activations offer promise but rely on dimensionality reduction that either lacks control over the compression/information-loss trade-off or produces excessively large representations for convolutional layers.
AI.method: The authors analyze dimensionality reductions in two state-of-the-art detection methods, develop a novel reduction method with controllable high-compression for convolutional layers, and extend the two detection methods to work with any dimensionality reduction technique.
AI.result: The proposed dimensionality reduction consistently outperforms or matches the strongest existing alternatives in out-of-distribution and adversarial attack detection, while achieving the highest compression among compared methods, thereby reducing computation and memory footprints.
AI.conclusion: The proposed controllable high-compression dimensionality reduction improves activation-based detection methods for CNNs, offering both strong detection performance and efficiency gains.

title: Chain of Spatial Thoughts: Modality-Agnostic Spatial Grounding for Vision Language Models
summary: Spatial understanding is fundamental to embodied intelligence, underpinning applications such as robotic manipulation, embodied navigation, and autonomous driving. Although recent vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved impressive performance on spatial reasoning benchmarks, state-of-the-art approaches typically rely on additional spatial encoders or architectural modifications during inference, increasing computational cost. We introduce Space Tokens, a lightweight, architecture-agnostic framework that equips VLMs with explicit continuous spatial representations without requiring additional inference-time modules. By distilling scene-level 3D geometry and object-centric spatial attributes into continuous latent tokens, our method enables these modalities to be directly incorporated into a chain-of-thought reasoning process, thereby improving the VLM's spatial reasoning capabilities. At the same time, the learned representations can be explicitly decoded to verify that they encode meaningful geometric information, while the unified token interface remains extensible to additional modalities. Experiments on VSI-Bench improve Qwen3-VL-8B by 4.3% and SenseNova-SI-1.3 by 1.3%, while achieving state-of-the-art performance on object size (79.2%) and room size estimation (75.7%). These results demonstrate that continuous spatial tokens provide an effective, interpretable, and computationally efficient mechanism for integrating geometric reasoning into large vision-language models.

AI.tldr: Space Tokens is a lightweight, architecture-agnostic framework that equips vision-language models (VLMs) with explicit continuous spatial representations via distilled 3D geometry and object-centric spatial attributes encoded as latent tokens. These tokens are incorporated directly into chain-of-thought reasoning without additional inference-time modules, improving spatial reasoning performance (e.g., +4.3% on VSI-Bench for Qwen3-VL-8B) while remaining interpretable and extensible to other modalities.
AI.motivation: Spatial understanding is critical for embodied intelligence, but state-of-the-art VLMs achieve strong spatial reasoning only by adding spatial encoders or architectural modifications at inference time, which increases computational cost. The authors seek a lightweight, architecture-agnostic solution that provides explicit spatial representations without extra inference-time overhead.
AI.method: Space Tokens distills scene-level 3D geometry and object-centric spatial attributes into continuous latent tokens. These tokens are integrated directly into the chain-of-thought reasoning process of a VLM via a unified token interface. The learned representations can be explicitly decoded to verify they encode meaningful geometric information, and the interface remains extensible to additional modalities.
AI.result: On VSI-Bench, Space Tokens improves Qwen3-VL-8B by 4.3% and SenseNova-SI-1.3 by 1.3%. It achieves state-of-the-art performance on object size estimation (79.2%) and room size estimation (75.7%).
AI.conclusion: Continuous spatial tokens provide an effective, interpretable, and computationally efficient mechanism for integrating geometric reasoning into large vision-language models, offering a practical alternative to heavier architectural modifications for spatial understanding tasks.

title: TRACE-GS: On-Policy Trajectory Distillation with Privileged Geometric Conditioning for Sparse-View 3DGS Restoration
summary: We present TRACE-GS, an on-policy trajectory distillation framework that leverages privileged geometric conditioning at training time, thereby adapting a diffusion prior to sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) restoration. Rather than pursuing increasingly sophisticated restoration architectures, we identify a more fundamental limitation shared by existing diffusion-based approaches: supervision at independently noised states does not cover those reached during inference. In sparse-view 3DGS, under-constrained geometry biases denoising from the outset, and the resulting deviations compound along the rollout. TRACE-GS instead performs on-policy trajectory distillation: a teacher conditioned on richer geometry from additional training views supplies targets along the sparse-view student's own rollout, aligning denoising directions and cross-view responses at each visited state. This training-only geometry places TRACE-GS in the learning using privileged information (LUPI) setting. At deployment, only the sparse-view student is retained, and its restored renderings serve as pseudo-observations for 3DGS refinement. To the best of our knowledge, TRACE-GS is the first to derive on-policy supervision from privileged geometry for sparse-view 3DGS restoration, achieving consistent gains and strong generalization across datasets and sparse-view settings.

AI.tldr: TRACE-GS is an on-policy trajectory distillation framework that uses privileged geometric conditioning during training to adapt a diffusion prior for sparse-view 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) restoration. A teacher conditioned on richer geometry from additional views supervises the student's own rollout, aligning denoising directions at each visited state. This is the first method to derive on-policy supervision from privileged geometry for this task, achieving consistent gains and strong generalization.
AI.motivation: Existing diffusion-based approaches for sparse-view 3DGS restoration suffer from a fundamental limitation: supervision at independently noised states does not cover the states reached during inference. Under-constrained geometry biases denoising from the outset, and deviations compound along the rollout, degrading performance.
AI.method: TRACE-GS performs on-policy trajectory distillation under the LUPI (learning using privileged information) setting. A teacher, conditioned on richer geometry from additional training views, supplies target denoising directions along the sparse-view student's own rollout, aligning both denoising trajectories and cross-view responses at each visited state. At deployment, only the sparse-view student is retained, and its restored renderings serve as pseudo-observations for 3DGS refinement.
AI.result: TRACE-GS achieves consistent performance gains and strong generalization across multiple datasets and sparse-view settings, establishing itself as the first work to derive on-policy supervision from privileged geometry for sparse-view 3DGS restoration.
AI.conclusion: Rather than pursuing increasingly sophisticated restoration architectures, TRACE-GS demonstrates that addressing the training-inference distribution mismatch via privileged-geometry-based on-policy trajectory distillation is a more fundamental and effective solution for sparse-view 3DGS restoration.

title: SeFaR: Semantic Feature-aware Robustness Testing of Deep Neural Networks
summary: Deep neural networks are increasingly deployed in safety-critical domains as perception modules, where failures are often caused due to rare and under-represented scenarios. This necessitates the need to evaluate the semantic robustness of perception models; conformance of behavior to high-level requirements over real-world perceptual variability. To address this, we propose SeFaR, a framework for systematic semantic-feature-centric testing of vision models. Given a natural-language requirement and a set of satisfying inputs, SeFaR evaluates robustness with respect to diverse realistic semantic variations that preserve requirement satisfaction. The approach employs a novel hierarchical concept model enabling structured exploration of the feature space and incorporation of domain knowledge via user-defined concepts. State-of-the-art diffusion and vision-language models are leveraged to generate photorealistic semantics-preserving perturbations and identification of previously unknown features impacting behavior. A feedback-driven adaptive process is adopted to generate interpretable failure-inducing semantic concepts along with corresponding test inputs. Evaluation on case studies demonstrates that the proposed framework effectively satisfies requirement preconditions while identifying requirement-independent features that influence model decisions, enabling it to both uncover faults and relate them to such features.

AI.tldr: SeFaR is a framework for systematic semantic-feature-centric testing of vision models, evaluating robustness against realistic semantic variations using hierarchical concept models, diffusion models, and vision-language models to generate interpretable failure-inducing test cases.
AI.motivation: Deep neural networks deployed in safety-critical domains often fail due to rare and under-represented scenarios. There is a need to evaluate the semantic robustness of perception models—i.e., conformance of behavior to high-level requirements over real-world perceptual variability.
AI.method: SeFaR employs a hierarchical concept model for structured exploration of feature space and domain knowledge integration. It uses state-of-the-art diffusion and vision-language models to generate photorealistic semantics-preserving perturbations, along with a feedback-driven adaptive process to produce interpretable failure-inducing semantic concepts and corresponding test inputs.
AI.result: Evaluation on case studies shows SeFaR effectively satisfies requirement preconditions while identifying requirement-independent features that influence model decisions, enabling both fault discovery and relating them to specific semantic features.
AI.conclusion: SeFaR demonstrates that systematic semantic-feature-centric testing can uncover faults in vision models and link them to interpretable real-world semantic concepts, contributing to more robust perception in safety-critical applications.

title: MRIComp4Flow: Compression of 3D Brain MRI for Training Multi-Modal Generative Models
summary: Large-scale multi-modal MRI datasets impose substantial storage and I/O costs, limiting the training of 3D generative models on commodity infrastructure. While lossy compression is known to preserve accuracy for discriminative segmentation networks, its effect on generative models, which must learn the full data distribution rather than a decision boundary, is unexplored. We study whether standard image codecs can effectively compress semantically rich brain tumor MRI while preserving the fidelity required to train and deploy a 3D MRI generative model. Each 3D volume is compressed with JPEG2000 or a near-lossless JPEG-LS pipeline. Next, a Wavelet Flow Matching model, conditioned on BraTS image sequences (T1n, T1c, T2, T2f), is trained on compressed data, and the resulting models are evaluated on the validation set. At a 20:1 compression ratio, synthesis quality is statistically equivalent to a model trained on uncompressed data within a pre-specified margin ($Δ$PSNR $<1$,dB, $Δ$SSIM $<0.02$; paired TOST $p=[[p]]$): mean PSNR is 27.3,dB vs. 27.0,dB and mean SSIM is 0.95 vs. 0.96 across modalities. Our results indicate that JPEG2000 compression is a practical step toward scalable 3D MRI generative modeling without degrading synthesis quality. The codebase is available at https://github.com/lisafis/MRIComp4Flow .

AI.tldr: This paper investigates whether standard lossy image codecs (JPEG2000, JPEG-LS) can compress large-scale 3D brain tumor MRI datasets for training generative models without degrading synthesis quality. A Wavelet Flow Matching model trained on 20:1 compressed data produces statistically equivalent results (PSNR 27.3 vs 27.0 dB, SSIM 0.95 vs 0.96) to one trained on uncompressed data, demonstrating that JPEG2000 compression is viable for scalable 3D MRI generative modeling.
AI.motivation: Large-scale multi-modal MRI datasets create significant storage and I/O bottlenecks that limit training 3D generative models on commodity hardware. While lossy compression is known to preserve accuracy for discriminative segmentation networks, it is unclear whether compressed data retains enough fidelity for generative models, which must learn the full data distribution rather than just a decision boundary.
AI.method: Each 3D brain tumor MRI volume is compressed using either JPEG2000 or a near-lossless JPEG-LS pipeline. A Wavelet Flow Matching model conditioned on BraTS image sequences (T1n, T1c, T2, T2f) is then trained on the compressed data and evaluated on a validation set. Statistical equivalence testing (paired TOST) is used to compare synthesis quality against models trained on uncompressed data.
AI.result: At a 20:1 compression ratio, synthesis quality from models trained on compressed data is statistically equivalent to models trained on uncompressed data within pre-specified margins (ΔPSNR < 1 dB, ΔSSIM < 0.02). Mean PSNR is 27.3 dB vs 27.0 dB and mean SSIM is 0.95 vs 0.96 across modalities.
AI.conclusion: JPEG2000 compression is a practical and effective step toward scalable 3D MRI generative modeling, as it substantially reduces storage and I/O costs without degrading synthesis quality. The codebase is publicly released.

title: Frozen Brain-MRI Foundation Models Are Site Fingerprints
summary: Frozen foundation-model (FM) embeddings are increasingly used as off-the-shelf brain-MRI representations, on the assumption that they capture anatomy. We audit what they actually encode and find that acquisition site is a large, intrinsic component of the representation. Across two independent cohorts (ABIDE-I, ABIDE-II), three frozen 3-D encoders (brain-pretrained, CT-pretrained, and randomly initialized), and every network depth, site is linearly decodable at roughly 0.9 balanced accuracy at deep layers, exceeding the decodability of every clinical or demographic variable (sex, age, autism diagnosis) at every layer. The effect is intrinsic rather than learned: a randomly initialized encoder is already a ~0.9 site classifier on both cohorts and across three architecture families (Swin, ViT, ResNet), and site is decodable at ~0.95 directly from the raw downsampled image with no encoder, so the fingerprint reflects low-level image statistics that any encoder preserves rather than a product of pretraining. Residualizing measured population covariates leaves site decodability essentially unchanged, indicating an acquisition- rather than population-driven effect. A nonlinear probe matches the linear one, so the fingerprint is fully linearly accessible. The site subspace is removable post hoc by iterative null-space projection or ComBat (site decodability 0.94 -> 0.07/0.00), and is a site-attribution concern for shared or federated embeddings; but for dense segmentation this removal is not free, because site and anatomy occupy an entangled linear subspace (a matched-rank random-direction projection is Dice-neutral, whereas removing the site subspace is destructive). We recommend site-audited use of frozen brain-MRI FMs and release an open audit toolkit.

AI.tldr: Frozen foundation-model embeddings for brain MRI are audited and found to primarily encode acquisition site as a large, intrinsic, linearly decodable component (~0.9 balanced accuracy), exceeding demographic/clinical variables. The effect stems from low-level image statistics present even in randomly initialized encoders and raw images, is resistant to covariate residualization, and while removable post hoc via null-space projection or ComBat, this removal degrades dense segmentation performance due to entangled site-anatomy subspaces. The authors recommend site-audited use of frozen brain-MRI FMs and release an audit toolkit.
AI.motivation: Frozen foundation-model embeddings are widely used as off-the-shelf brain-MRI representations under the assumption they faithfully capture anatomy, yet this assumption has not been rigorously audited. This paper systematically investigates what these embeddings actually encode, particularly whether acquisition site confounds are present at a level that undermines their validity.
AI.method: The authors audit three frozen 3-D encoders (brain-pretrained, CT-pretrained, randomly initialized) across two independent cohorts (ABIDE-I, ABIDE-II) and multiple architecture families (Swin, ViT, ResNet). They measure linear decodability of site vs. clinical/demographic variables at every network depth, test randomly initialized encoders and raw downsampled images to isolate intrinsic effects, perform covariate residualization, compare nonlinear vs. linear probes, and evaluate post-hoc site removal via iterative null-space projection and ComBat (including Dice-based segmentation benchmarks with matched-rank random-direction projections as controls).
AI.result: Site is linearly decodable at ~0.9 balanced accuracy at deep layers across all encoders and cohorts, exceeding all clinical/demographic variables. The effect is intrinsic: randomly initialized encoders achieve ~0.9 and raw downsampled images yield ~0.95. Residualizing population covariates doesn't change site decodability. Site removal (null-space projection or ComBat) reduces decodability from 0.94 to 0.07/0.00, but unlike matched-rank random projections, this removal is destructive for dense segmentation because site and anatomy occupy an entangled linear subspace.
AI.conclusion: Acquisition site is a dominant, intrinsic, linearly accessible component of frozen brain-MRI FM embeddings, driven by low-level image statistics rather than pretraining or population demographics. While the site subspace is removable post hoc, doing so comes at a cost for segmentation tasks due to site-anatomy entanglement. The authors recommend site-audited use of frozen brain-MRI FMs and provide an open audit toolkit to support this practice.

title: UniMod: Enhancing Multi-Modal Medical Diagnosis through Cross-Modality and Within-Modality Alignment
comment: Accepted to ACM Multimedia 2026 (MM '26). 10 pages, 7 figures, 5 tables. Code: https://github.com/futurespyhi/UniMod
summary: Multi-modal learning combining medical images and clinical text is promising for disease diagnosis. However, standard multi-modal training leads to shortcut learning: models exploit the easier modality (e.g., diagnostic cues in text) while neglecting harder-to-learn features (e.g., subtle visual patterns). We propose UniMod, a framework that mitigates shortcut learning by requiring each modality to predict the diagnosis on its own. It supervises image-only, text-only, and multi-modal classification simultaneously, so each modality must extract diagnostic features. We add cross-modality alignment for knowledge transfer and within-modality supervised contrastive alignment over same-diagnosis patients. On Harvard-Glaucoma, UniMod reaches 0.850 AUC, outperforming OGM-GE and Gradient Blending by 1.6-1.8%; on CheXpert Plus, it reaches 0.966 AUC, surpassing them by over 5%. UniMod also extends to 5-class multi-label diagnosis without architectural change, improving mean AUC by 0.097 over CGGM.

AI.tldr: UniMod is a multi-modal learning framework that mitigates shortcut learning in disease diagnosis by requiring each modality (image and text) to independently predict the diagnosis, combined with cross-modality alignment and supervised contrastive learning. It achieves 0.850 AUC on Harvard-Glaucoma and 0.966 AUC on CheXpert Plus, outperforming existing shortcut-mitigation methods.
AI.motivation: Standard multi-modal training in medical AI suffers from shortcut learning, where models exploit the easier modality (e.g., text diagnostic cues) while neglecting harder-to-learn features (e.g., subtle visual patterns in images), degrading overall diagnostic performance.
AI.method: UniMod simultaneously supervises image-only, text-only, and multi-modal classifications so each modality must extract diagnostic features independently. It incorporates cross-modality alignment for knowledge transfer and within-modality supervised contrastive alignment over same-diagnosis patients.
AI.result: On Harvard-Glaucoma, UniMod reaches 0.850 AUC, outperforming OGM-GE and Gradient Blending by 1.6-1.8%. On CheXpert Plus, it reaches 0.966 AUC, surpassing them by over 5%. It also extends to 5-class multi-label diagnosis, improving mean AUC by 0.097 over CGGM.
AI.conclusion: UniMod effectively prevents shortcut learning in multi-modal medical diagnosis by compelling each modality to independently learn diagnostic features, leading to significant performance improvements across glaucoma and chest X-ray datasets, including multi-label settings.

title: From Detection to Understanding: TAR and TAR-Bench for Multi-Task Traffic Anomaly Reasoning
summary: We present TAR (Traffic Anomaly Reasoning) and TAR-Bench datasets, resources for training and evaluating video-language models beyond anomaly detection. TAR contains 44,040 chain-of-thought training annotations across 10 tasks for 3,670 CCTV videos ($\sim$26 hours) from eight public datasets. Its evaluation component, TAR-Bench, contains 960 human-curated test annotations for 80 held-out clips trimmed from 17 public YouTube videos. TAR's training annotations are produced with MAVEN, which consolidates multi-scale video evidence into structured event descriptions before generating question-answer pairs and reasoning traces. On TAR-Bench, eleven vision-language models reveal that strong question-answering accuracy does not reliably predict temporal or scene reasoning ability. Multi-task fine-tuning on TAR yields consistent gains, with the full 10-task model improving aggregate score by 21.4 points over its zero-shot baseline. TAR and TAR-Bench provide the official training and in-domain evaluation data for AI City Challenge 2026 Track 3. The dataset is available at https://huggingface.co/datasets/nvidia/PhysicalAI-Traffic-Anomaly-Reasoning

AI.tldr: The paper introduces TAR (Traffic Anomaly Reasoning) datasets for training and evaluating video-language models on traffic anomaly reasoning tasks, containing 44,040 chain-of-thought annotations across 10 tasks and 3,670 CCTV videos, plus TAR-Bench with 960 human-curated test annotations. The models show that QA accuracy doesn't reliably predict reasoning ability, and multi-task fine-tuning improves performance by 21.4 points.
AI.motivation: To push video-language models beyond simple anomaly detection toward complex reasoning about traffic anomalies, addressing the gap between basic detection capabilities and higher-order temporal/scene reasoning skills, and providing standardized training/evaluation resources for this purpose.
AI.method: TAR uses MAVEN to consolidate multi-scale video evidence into structured event descriptions before generating question-answer pairs and reasoning traces. The system includes 10 reasoning tasks across 3,670 CCTV videos from 8 public datasets, with human-curated evaluation annotations for 80 held-out clips from 17 public YouTube videos.
AI.result: Eleven vision-language models evaluated on TAR-Bench show that strong question-answering accuracy does not reliably predict temporal or scene reasoning ability. Multi-task fine-tuning on TAR yields consistent gains, with the full 10-task model improving aggregate score by 21.4 points over zero-shot baseline.
AI.conclusion: TAR and TAR-Bench provide the official training and in-domain evaluation data for AI City Challenge 2026 Track 3, offering valuable resources for advancing video-language model reasoning capabilities in traffic anomaly domains.

title: ENCORE: Efficient Noise Context-Aware Representation for Low-Dose CT Denoising
summary: While deep learning-based denoising has become widely adopted in low-dose CT, conventional models use generic architectures designed for natural images, failing to account for non-stationary and spatially correlated CT noise characteristics. To address this, we propose an Efficient Noise COntext-aware REpresentation (ENCORE) framework that explicitly leverages CT noise characteristics and anatomical features. First, we reformulate the noise synthesis procedure based on a realistic noise distribution beyond the conventional Gaussian approximation, establishing a rigorous foundation for training pair generation. Next, we extract local noise power and correlation contexts to guide the denoising process. To fully leverage the potential of noise context, we propose a FlyingConv module, which adaptively changes convolution weights for each local image region. Notably, our approach demonstrates substantial gains in both denoising quality and computational efficiency. Furthermore, manipulating the intensity of the noise context maps at inference time enables zero-shot conditional denoising, allowing for dynamic control over the output image texture. The entire pipeline is available at https://github.com/minwoo-yu/ENCORE.git

AI.tldr: The paper proposes ENCORE, a noise context-aware denoising framework for low-dose CT that leverages realistic noise distributions (beyond Gaussian), extracts local noise power and correlation contexts, and uses a FlyingConv module for adaptive convolution weights, achieving superior denoising quality and computational efficiency with zero-shot conditional denoising capability.
AI.motivation: Conventional deep learning denoising models use generic architectures designed for natural images, which fail to account for the non-stationary and spatially correlated noise characteristics specific to CT imaging.
AI.method: 1) Reformulates noise synthesis based on realistic noise distribution beyond conventional Gaussian approximation for training pair generation. 2) Extracts local noise power and correlation contexts to guide denoising. 3) Proposes FlyingConv module that adaptively changes convolution weights for each local image region based on noise context.
AI.result: The approach demonstrates substantial gains in both denoising quality and computational efficiency, and enables zero-shot conditional denoising via intensity manipulation of noise context maps at inference time.
AI.conclusion: Explicitly leveraging CT noise characteristics and anatomical features through noise context-aware representations significantly improves low-dose CT denoising, with the added benefit of dynamic output texture control at inference.

title: CasDeblurGS: Cascaded 2D-to-3D Multi-View Consistency for 3D Gaussian Splatting from Two Blurry Images
comment: Accepted to the ECCV 2026 MUSTCV Workshop. Project page: https://haeyun-choi.github.io/Cascaded2D3D_page/
summary: Free-viewpoint 3D scene media is increasingly important for immersive applications, yet practical capture often suffers from severe view sparsity and motion blur. Although neural rendering has advanced sparse-view synthesis, existing blur-aware methods typically require substantial multi-view redundancy, accurate camera poses, or costly per-scene optimization. We address a stringent yet practical setting: reconstructing a coherent 3D scene from only two motion-blurred images with known intrinsics, without input-view poses, auxiliary sharp images, or per-scene test-time optimization. To this end, we propose CasDeblurGS, a cascaded framework that progressively recovers reliable cross-view information from local 2D correspondences to global 3D guidance. Stage 1 constructs locally reliable guidance through occlusion-aware correspondence filtering, while Stage 2 aggregates the intermediate restorations into a provisional pose-free 3D Gaussian representation whose input-view re-renders provide dense global guidance for final restoration. The resulting views enable a more coherent 3D representation and higher-quality novel-view synthesis. Experiments on real-world and synthetic Deblur-NeRF scenes show consistent gains over strong baselines, improving PSNR by 1.19 dB and 2.11 dB, respectively. Progressive ablations, cross-view correspondence visualization, and camera reprojection analysis further demonstrate improvements in both rendering quality and multi-view geometric consistency.

AI.tldr: CasDeblurGS is a cascaded framework that reconstructs a coherent 3D scene from only two motion-blurred images without input-view poses, auxiliary sharp images, or per-scene test-time optimization, progressively recovering cross-view information from local 2D correspondences to global 3D guidance for improved novel-view synthesis.
AI.motivation: Practical 3D scene capture often suffers from view sparsity and motion blur, but existing blur-aware neural rendering methods require multi-view redundancy, accurate camera poses, or costly per-scene optimization. The paper addresses a stringent yet practical setting: reconstructing from only two motion-blurred images with known intrinsics, without poses, sharp images, or test-time optimization.
AI.method: CasDeblurGS uses a cascaded framework with two stages. Stage 1 constructs locally reliable guidance via occlusion-aware correspondence filtering. Stage 2 aggregates intermediate restorations into a provisional pose-free 3D Gaussian representation, whose input-view re-renders provide dense global guidance for final restoration.
AI.result: Experiments on real-world and synthetic Deblur-NeRF scenes show consistent gains over strong baselines, improving PSNR by 1.19 dB and 2.11 dB respectively. Progressive ablations, cross-view correspondence visualization, and camera reprojection analysis demonstrate improvements in both rendering quality and multi-view geometric consistency.
AI.conclusion: The cascaded local-to-global guidance framework enables coherent 3D scene reconstruction and higher-quality novel-view synthesis from extremely sparse and blurred inputs, improving both rendering quality and multi-view geometric consistency.

title: Towards Unified Dynamic Face Landmark Detection
comment: 9 pages, 6 figures in Main Paper. 13 pages, 3 figures in Appendix
summary: Although advancements in face landmark detection (FLD) methods continue to push performance boundaries, they overlook two major functional limitations: (1) different network parameters need to be trained independently for each ``$N$-point'' benchmark dataset, and (2) a model trained on an ``$N$-point'' dataset reliably outputs only the $N$ landmarks. In our work, we first conceptualize Face Part-Anchored Landmark Positions (FPALPs), wherein each landmark is treated as a progression value between zero (start) and one (end) along a face part's contour. Every landmark can be expressed in the FPALP format, irrespective of its source dataset, hence unlocking the ability to unify all ``$N$-point'' datasets into a single dataset. Secondly, we represent each landmark with an FPALP-based query, refine it progressively with a cross-modality decoder, and predict its coordinates based on the final representation. Our approach, called Unified Dynamic FLD, embodies these two design choices and streamlines the landmark detection pipeline by enabling (1) a single model to learn on any number of ``$N$-point'' datasets, and (2) yield any number of specific landmark predictions by loading the designated landmark queries at runtime. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets show that our method delivers these benefits while remaining competitive with, and in several cases outperforming existing state-of-the-art methods.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces Unified Dynamic FLD, a face landmark detection method that unifies all N-point benchmark datasets into a single training set using Face Part-Anchored Landmark Positions (FPALPs) and uses FPALP-based queries with a cross-modality decoder to enable one model to predict any number of landmarks dynamically at runtime.
AI.motivation: Existing face landmark detection methods have two major limitations: (1) separate network parameters must be trained independently for each N-point benchmark dataset, and (2) a model trained on an N-point dataset can only reliably output those N specific landmarks.
AI.method: The approach has two key components. First, it introduces Face Part-Anchored Landmark Positions (FPALPs), where each landmark is represented as a progression value between 0 and 1 along a face part's contour, allowing landmarks from any dataset to be expressed uniformly and enabling unification of all N-point datasets. Second, it represents each landmark as an FPALP-based query, refines it progressively with a cross-modality decoder, and predicts coordinates from the final representation.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on multiple benchmark datasets demonstrate that the method delivers both benefits (unified training across datasets and dynamic landmark prediction) while remaining competitive with, and in several cases outperforming, existing state-of-the-art methods.
AI.conclusion: The Unified Dynamic FLD approach streamlines the landmark detection pipeline by enabling a single model to learn from any number of N-point datasets and yield any number of specific landmark predictions by simply loading designated landmark queries at runtime.

title: FormStruct-Bench:A Hierarchical and Diagnostic Benchmark for Table-Form Document Structure Recognition
summary: Transforming table-form documents into machine-processable records requires recovering not only their visible content but also the multilevel structure that organizes it. However, existing benchmarks evaluate either holistic document outputs or conventional table grids, and their aggregate scores provide little insight into where structural failures occur. We introduce FormStruct-Bench, a hierarchical and diagnostic benchmark that evaluates table-form document structure recognition at both the document level and progressively finer component levels, allowing aggregate performance to be traced back to specific structural failure modes. To construct auditable ground truth at scale, we annotate 70 reusable templates and expand them into 7,000 verified instances through a provenance-preserving Director--Artist--Verifier pipeline; all 1,100 instances in the template-disjoint test set additionally receive human review. Our evaluation protocol uses five primary metrics and three structure-specific diagnostics across page, schema, and component levels, together with slices over difficulty, structural constraints, and visual degradation. Across 14 API-hosted and locally deployable systems plus two SFT variants, the best document-level score reaches 83.85%, whereas the best reported fine-grained structural score remains below 18%. These results reveal a pronounced gap between reading document content and recovering the hierarchy and regional organization required for reliable table-form understanding.

AI.tldr: FormStruct-Bench is a hierarchical, diagnostic benchmark for evaluating table-form document structure recognition, built from 70 templates expanded into 7,000 verified instances via a provenance-preserving pipeline. Testing 14 systems plus 2 SFT variants, it reveals a large gap between content reading (83.85% best) and fine-grained structural recovery (<18%), showing that existing models struggle with multilevel hierarchy and regional organization.
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks evaluate either holistic document outputs or conventional table grids, and their aggregate scores fail to localize where structural failures occur in table-form document understanding. There is a need for a benchmark that traces performance degradation back to specific structural failure modes.
AI.method: The authors construct FormStruct-Bench with 70 reusable templates expanded into 7,000 verified instances using a Director-Artist-Verifier pipeline that preserves provenance. The test set (1,100 template-disjoint instances) receives human review. Evaluation uses five primary metrics and three structure-specific diagnostics across page, schema, and component levels, with slices over difficulty, structural constraints, and visual degradation.
AI.result: Across 14 API-hosted and locally deployable systems plus two SFT variants, the best document-level score reaches 83.85%, while the best fine-grained structural score remains below 18%, revealing a pronounced performance gap between content reading and structural recovery.
AI.conclusion: Current table-form understanding systems can read document content reasonably well but fail to reliably recover the multilevel hierarchy and regional organization needed for robust table-form understanding, highlighting a critical gap that FormStruct-Bench exposes and can diagnose.

title: A second-order theory of texture for depth from focus
summary: We present a theory of textured appearance of optically rough surfaces based on wave optics, emphasizing the role of texture for passive depth from focus. Our theory shows that even surfaces that traditional computer vision would consider textureless can produce textured appearance, due to subjective speckle from surface microgeometry. We analyze the properties of this second-order texture, and show that we can enhance its contrast under natural ambient lighting by simply using a narrowband spectral filter. Doing so results in dramatic improvements in passive depth reconstruction of seemingly textureless scenes, as we demonstrate through extensive theory, simulations, and real-world experiments.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a wave-optics-based theory explaining how optically rough surfaces, even those considered textureless in traditional computer vision, produce textured appearance via subjective speckle from surface microgeometry. The authors show this second-order texture can be enhanced under natural lighting using narrowband spectral filters, leading to dramatic improvements in passive depth-from-focus reconstruction, validated through theory, simulations, and real-world experiments.
AI.motivation: Traditional computer vision treats many optically rough surfaces as textureless, which severely limits passive depth from focus methods. The authors aim to show that these surfaces actually possess a hidden texture signature arising from wave-optics effects (speckle), and that this can be exploited for improved depth reconstruction.
AI.method: The authors develop a wave-optics theory of textured appearance for optically rough surfaces, demonstrating that subjective speckle from surface microgeometry generates measurable texture. They propose enhancing this second-order texture contrast under natural ambient lighting by employing narrowband spectral filters, and validate their approach through theoretical analysis, simulations, and real-world experiments.
AI.result: The theory reveals that seemingly textureless surfaces do produce textured appearance via subjective speckle. Using narrowband spectral filtering significantly enhances the contrast of this second-order texture, resulting in dramatic improvements in passive depth reconstruction accuracy for scenes that would otherwise be considered textureless.
AI.conclusion: Optically rough surfaces contain exploitable microgeometry-driven texture that traditional vision models miss. Narrowband spectral filtering is a simple yet effective way to reveal this texture under natural lighting, enabling substantially better passive depth from focus performance on previously "textureless" scenes.

title: DriveVLA-M0: Failure-Aware Memory Augmentation for Autonomous Driving
summary: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have recently emerged as a promising paradigm for end-to-end autonomous driving by enabling unified reasoning across perception, language, and planning. However, existing approaches lack mechanisms to exploit past failures or adapt to distribution shifts, causing the model to persistently underperform on similar scenarios where it has previously failed. In this paper, we propose DriveVLA-M0, a retrieval-augmented VLA with failure-aware latent memory. We construct a latent memory pool that stores failure cases along with their structure scene representations and expert trajectory labels, and design a dedicated Retrieve Model that decouples static road structure and dynamic agent interactions to enable structurally grounded retrieval. At inference time, retrieved cases are injected into the model via a lightweight decoupled LoRA-based test-time training (TTT) mechanism, allowing targeted and scenario-specific correction without modifying the backbone. Extensive experiments on NAVSIMv1 and NAVSIMv2 benchmark demonstrate that our approach consistently outperforms prior methods, achieving 94.1 PDMS on Navtest and 47.0 EPDMS on Navhard with only 26.44 ms TTT backward latency overhead. Furthermore, we show that DriveVLA-M0 scales effectively with additional memory, enabling training-free performance gains through memory expansion. The code is available at https://github.com/ZebinX/DriveVLA-M0.

AI.tldr: DriveVLA-M0 is a retrieval-augmented Vision-Language-Action model for autonomous driving that stores past failure cases in a latent memory pool and retrieves them at inference time via a decoupled LoRA-based test-time training mechanism, achieving 94.1 PDMS on Navtest and 47.0 EPDMS on Navhard with only 26.44 ms TTT backward latency overhead.
AI.motivation: Existing VLA models for autonomous driving lack mechanisms to exploit past failures or adapt to distribution shifts, causing them to persistently underperform on similar scenarios where they have previously failed.
AI.method: The authors construct a latent memory pool storing failure cases with structure scene representations and expert trajectory labels. A dedicated Retrieve Model decouples static road structure and dynamic agent interactions for structurally grounded retrieval. At inference time, retrieved cases are injected via a lightweight decoupled LoRA-based test-time training (TTT) mechanism for targeted, scenario-specific correction without modifying the backbone.
AI.result: DriveVLA-M0 consistently outperforms prior methods on NAVSIMv1 and NAVSIMv2 benchmarks, achieving 94.1 PDMS on Navtest and 47.0 EPDMS on Navhard with only 26.44 ms TTT backward latency overhead. The model also scales effectively with additional memory, enabling training-free performance gains through memory expansion.
AI.conclusion: Retrieval-augmented VLA with failure-aware latent memory provides an effective mechanism for adapting to past failures and distribution shifts in autonomous driving, with scalable memory expansion enabling continued performance gains without additional training.

title: GeoSeg-OV: Bridging Geospatial Gaps with Structural Guidance for Open-Vocabulary Remote Sensing Segmentation
summary: Open-vocabulary remote sensing segmentation has recently emerged as a promising paradigm that enables pixel-level recognition of arbitrary categories specified by natural language, including classes unseen during training. However, geospatial domain shifts caused by heterogeneous regions, spatial resolutions, and acquisition platforms weaken visual-text matching and limit cross-dataset generalization. Recent attempts have begun to incorporate auxiliary vision foundation models (VFMs), typically coupling their features with text embeddings as additional matching evidence. However, this strategy may introduce inconsistent matching signals while leaving the structure-sensitive representations of VFMs insufficiently exploited. We therefore propose GeoSeg-OV, which decouples auxiliary VFM features from visual-text matching and repurposes them as structural guidance for cost aggregation and decoding. GeoSeg-OV constructs an orientation-robust cost volume from multi-rotation CLIP features, while a frozen VFM extracts multi-scale structure-sensitive features in parallel. We propose Structure-Guided Aggregation (SGA), which integrates cost tokens and CLIP semantic guidance with VFM-derived pairwise structural biases for coherent spatial propagation, followed by text-conditioned class-wise reasoning. We further introduce Cost-Aware Decoding (CAD) to adaptively refine and fuse multi-scale semantic and structural guidance based on the current decoder context. On the global High-Resolution Land Cover (HRLC) benchmark spanning seven datasets across six continents, GeoSeg-OV outperforms the state-of-the-art by +2.5 and +2.7 average mIoU under two training settings. A large-scale zero-shot case study further demonstrates its generalization across geographic domains and category systems without target-domain annotations or retraining.

AI.tldr: GeoSeg-OV is an open-vocabulary remote sensing segmentation model that decouples auxiliary vision foundation model (VFM) features from visual-text matching and repurposes them as structural guidance for cost aggregation and decoding, achieving state-of-the-art results on the global HRLC benchmark.
AI.motivation: Open-vocabulary remote sensing segmentation suffers from geospatial domain shifts (heterogeneous regions, resolutions, acquisition platforms) that weaken visual-text matching. Prior work couples VFM features with text embeddings as additional matching evidence, but this introduces inconsistent matching signals and underutilizes the structure-sensitive representations of VFMs.
AI.method: GeoSeg-OV constructs an orientation-robust cost volume from multi-rotation CLIP features while a frozen VFM extracts multi-scale structure-sensitive features in parallel. It introduces Structure-Guided Aggregation (SGA) which integrates cost tokens and CLIP semantic guidance with VFM-derived pairwise structural biases for coherent spatial propagation, followed by text-conditioned class-wise reasoning. Additionally, Cost-Aware Decoding (CAD) adaptively refines and fuses multi-scale semantic and structural guidance based on the current decoder context.
AI.result: On the HRLC benchmark spanning seven datasets across six continents, GeoSeg-OV outperforms state-of-the-art by +2.5 and +2.7 average mIoU under two training settings. A large-scale zero-shot case study further demonstrates its generalization across geographic domains and category systems without target-domain annotations or retraining.
AI.conclusion: Decoupling VFM features from visual-text matching and repurposing them purely as structural guidance is more effective than coupling them as additional matching evidence, leading to improved cross-dataset generalization in open-vocabulary remote sensing segmentation.

title: Lesion-Aware Adaptive Fourier Neural Operator for CT-to-PSMA PET Synthesis in Prostate Cancer
summary: Deep learning models that synthesize PET from CT or MRI can reduce patient dose and scanner demand, but are typically optimized with global losses such as L1 or mean squared error (MSE) that treat all voxels similarly. In whole-body PSMA-PET, tumor voxels occupy only a small fraction of the volume, yet carry the clinically relevant activity signal; as a result, models can achieve high structural similarity index measure (SSIM) and peak signal-to-noise ratio (PSNR) while still underestimating lesion activity or failing to preserve tumor-specific structure. Radiomics provides biologically meaningful descriptors of tumor intensity and texture, but direct radiomics conditioning is time-consuming because it requires feature extraction from delineated lesion regions. We propose LAFNO, a Lesion-Aware Adaptive Fourier Neural Operator for CT-to-PSMA-PET synthesis that replaces high-dimensional radiomics conditioning with two efficient CT-derived proxy channels. Motivated by radiomics analysis of PSMA-avid tumor core and peritumoral regions, LAFNO uses a contrast proxy for local density variation and a disorder proxy for local texture heterogeneity, both injected into the model bottleneck. LAFNO combines whole-volume reconstruction with lesion-level total lesion activity (TLA), tumor-core contrast, and peritumoral supervision. We evaluated LAFNO against four baseline architectures on the TCIA PSMA-PET-CT-Lesions dataset.
