LAFNO remained competitive on whole-volume image quality, achieving SSIM of 0.960 and 0.938 for 18F- and 68Ga-PSMA, respectively, while reducing per-patient TLA error to 48.3% and 64.0% for 18F- and 68Ga-PSMA, respectively, and achieving the highest tumor-core radiomics reproducibility across all feature classes for both tracers. Peritumoral reproducibility remained tracer-dependent, indicating that biological fidelity in synthetic PSMA-PET remains challenging.

AI.tldr: LAFNO is a Lesion-Aware Adaptive Fourier Neural Operator for CT-to-PSMA-PET synthesis that uses two CT-derived proxy channels (contrast and disorder) instead of expensive radiomics conditioning, combines whole-volume reconstruction with lesion-level supervision, and achieves competitive image quality with better lesion activity estimation and tumor-core radiomics reproducibility than baseline models.
AI.motivation: Existing PET synthesis models optimized with global losses (L1/MSE) treat all voxels equally, but in whole-body PSMA-PET, tumor voxels are a tiny fraction yet carry the clinically relevant signal. Models can achieve high SSIM/PSNR while underestimating lesion activity or losing tumor-specific structure. Radiomics conditioning is biologically meaningful but requires time-consuming feature extraction from delineated lesions.
AI.method: LAFNO replaces high-dimensional radiomics conditioning with two efficient CT-derived proxy channels: a contrast proxy for local density variation and a disorder proxy for local texture heterogeneity, both injected into the model bottleneck. It combines whole-volume reconstruction with lesion-level supervision including total lesion activity (TLA), tumor-core contrast, and peritumoral losses, built on an adaptive Fourier neural operator architecture.
AI.result: On the TCIA PSMA-PET-CT-Lesions dataset, LAFNO achieved SSIM of 0.960 and 0.938 for 18F- and 68Ga-PSMA, competitive with baselines, while reducing per-patient TLA error to 48.3% and 64.0%, and achieving the highest tumor-core radiomics reproducibility across all feature classes for both tracers. Peritumoral reproducibility remained tracer-dependent.
AI.conclusion: LAFNO demonstrates that efficient proxy channels can substitute for expensive radiomics conditioning, improving lesion-level fidelity without sacrificing whole-volume image quality. However, peritumoral biological fidelity in synthetic PSMA-PET remains challenging and tracer-dependent.

title: DynaPPI: A Large-scale Dynamic Protein Dataset for AI-driven Advances in Protein Interactomics
comment: 9 pages, 1 figure, 39th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2025) Workshop: AI4Science
summary: Diffusion models have been widely explored in protein backbone generation due to their powerful generation capabilities.However, in today's AI-driven biological research, predicting the structure of unknown multi-chain protein aggregates (called "complexes" in biology) remains an unsolved challenge.This is because existing static or dynamic protein datasets focus solely on static snapshots or single-entity trajectories, neglecting the dynamic process of multiple monomers forming complexes.To alleviate this dilemma, we present DynaPPI, a dynamic protein dataset comprising molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories of protein complex formation from dissociated chains to the bound state, as a pivotal resource to bridge the gap between static structural biology and the inherently temporal nature of dynamic molecular interactions.Benefiting from this dataset, diffusion models can explicitly learn the dynamic binding trajectories of known complexes and accurately predict the structures of unknown complexes based on their diverse generative properties, thereby further catalyzing AI-driven structural biology and protein interactomics.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces DynaPPI, a novel dynamic protein dataset containing molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories of protein complex formation—from dissociated chains to the bound state. This dataset bridges the gap between static structural biology and the temporal nature of molecular interactions, enabling diffusion models to learn dynamic binding trajectories and predict structures of unknown multi-chain protein complexes.
AI.motivation: Predicting the structure of unknown multi-chain protein complexes remains an unsolved challenge because existing static or dynamic protein datasets focus only on static snapshots or single-entity trajectories, neglecting the dynamic process of multiple monomers forming complexes. This limitation hampers AI-driven biological research in protein complex structure prediction.
AI.method: The paper presents DynaPPI, a dynamic protein dataset comprising molecular dynamics (MD) trajectories of protein complex formation, capturing the transition from dissociated chains to the bound state. This dataset enables diffusion models to explicitly learn dynamic binding trajectories of known complexes and leverage their generative capabilities for accurate prediction of unknown complex structures.
AI.result: By leveraging the DynaPPI dataset, diffusion models can explicitly learn dynamic binding trajectories of known complexes and accurately predict the structures of unknown complexes, based on their diverse generative properties.
AI.conclusion: DynaPPI serves as a pivotal resource to bridge the gap between static structural biology and the inherently temporal nature of dynamic molecular interactions, further catalyzing AI-driven structural biology and protein interactomics.

title: MammoMix: Leveraging Mixture of Experts for Robust Mammogram Breast Detection
comment: Australasian Joint Conference on Artificial Intelligence 2025
summary: Breast lesion detection in mammography remains a challenging task due to variations in image quality, lesion appearance, and population demographics across datasets. While current object detectors such as YOLO and DETR achieve strong results on individual datasets, their performance often degrades when trained on or applied across heterogeneous sources. To address this, we propose MammoMix, a novel framework based on Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) paradigm for robust and generalizable lesion detection. In MammoMix, each expert model is trained on a specific domain, allowing it to specialize in distinct characteristics of its source data. A gating mechanism adaptively weighs contributions from each expert based on input image, combining their outputs to enable domain-adaptive inference. To improve reliability, we further incorporate a calibration module, MoCAE, which adjusts confidence scores to reflect true predictive uncertainty. We evaluate MammoMix on 3 public mammography datasets: CSAW, DDSM, and DMID, covering diverse clinical settings. Results show that MammoMix outperforms baseline detectors in both average precision and reliability, particularly on datasets with greater variability. Our findings demonstrate that expert specialization and calibrated ensemble fusion significantly enhance model generalization and robustness. MammoMix offers a promising step toward dependable AI-assisted breast cancer screening across real-world clinical domains.

AI.tldr: MammoMix is a Mixture-of-Experts framework for robust breast lesion detection in mammography, where expert models specialize in distinct source domains and a gating mechanism adaptively fuses their outputs. A calibration module (MoCAE) adjusts confidence scores for better reliability. Evaluated on three public datasets (CSAW, DDSM, DMID), it outperforms baseline detectors in both average precision and reliability.
AI.motivation: Breast lesion detection in mammography is challenging due to variations in image quality, lesion appearance, and demographics across datasets. Existing detectors like YOLO and DETR perform well on individual datasets but degrade when applied across heterogeneous sources, highlighting the need for robust and generalizable detection methods.
AI.method: MammoMix employs a Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) paradigm where each expert is trained on a specific domain to specialize in its source data characteristics. A gating mechanism adaptively weighs expert contributions based on the input image for domain-adaptive inference, and a calibration module (MoCAE) adjusts confidence scores to reflect true predictive uncertainty.
AI.result: Evaluated on three public mammography datasets (CSAW, DDSM, DMID), MammoMix outperforms baseline detectors in both average precision and reliability, with particularly strong improvements on datasets exhibiting greater variability.
AI.conclusion: Expert specialization combined with calibrated ensemble fusion significantly enhances model generalization and robustness across diverse clinical domains, offering a promising direction for dependable AI-assisted breast cancer screening.

title: Stream Forcing: Constructing Unified Training Trajectory for Robust Streaming Video Generation
summary: Streaming video generation holds strong potential for world modeling, where future frames must be inferred online sequentially to form a continuous video stream. However, streaming video diffusion models introduce a fundamental train-inference mismatch: inference follows a specialized denoising order, whereas advanced training strategies typically require diverse noise-level configurations. To address this trade-off between train-inference consistency and training coverage, we reformulate the video diffusion sampling as a frame-indexed stochastic process over noise levels. Within this stochastic process space, we construct a continuous training trajectory along which the sampling schedule progressively evolves from independent sampling to inference-consistent sampling. We further introduce a joint calibration algorithm and a temporal correlative sampling algorithm to ensure trajectory smoothness and cross-frame correlation. Building on these designs, we propose Stream Forcing, a unified training framework for streaming video generation that balances training sufficiency and inference efficiency. Extensive experiments demonstrate that Stream Forcing significantly improves generation quality with a 36.6% FVD improvement on the UCF-101 benchmark. Furthermore, our method facilitates robust zero-shot extrapolation to long-horizon video generation with a 27.9% FVD improvement on the UCF-101 benchmark.

AI.tldr: Stream Forcing is a unified training framework for streaming video generation that reformulates video diffusion sampling as a frame-indexed stochastic process over noise levels, resolving the train-inference mismatch in streaming diffusion models. It achieves 36.6% and 27.9% FVD improvements on UCF-101 for generation quality and zero-shot long-horizon extrapolation respectively.
AI.motivation: Streaming video diffusion models suffer from a fundamental train-inference mismatch: inference requires a specialized denoising order for online sequential generation, but advanced training strategies typically need diverse noise-level configurations. This creates a trade-off between train-inference consistency and training coverage that needs to be resolved.
AI.method: The paper reformulates video diffusion sampling as a frame-indexed stochastic process over noise levels. Within this stochastic process space, they construct a continuous training trajectory where the sampling schedule progressively evolves from independent sampling to inference-consistent sampling. They introduce a joint calibration algorithm and a temporal correlative sampling algorithm to ensure trajectory smoothness and cross-frame correlation, forming the Stream Forcing unified training framework.
AI.result: Stream Forcing achieves a 36.6% FVD improvement on the UCF-101 benchmark for generation quality, and enables robust zero-shot extrapolation to long-horizon video generation with a 27.9% FVD improvement on UCF-101.
AI.conclusion: Stream Forcing successfully balances training sufficiency and inference efficiency for streaming video generation, significantly improving generation quality and enabling robust long-horizon zero-shot extrapolation, demonstrating strong potential for world modeling.

title: FUSE: Frame-Unified Stress Estimation from Facial Video
comment: The paper has been accepted at: IEEE | 2026 9th International Conference on Pattern Recognition and Artificial Intelligence (PRAI 2026)
summary: Automatic stress detection from facial video offers a practical path to non-intrusive affect monitoring, yet existing video-based approaches commonly decompose full recordings into short temporal windows before classification. This design introduces additional choices regarding window length, overlap, and aggregation, while limiting direct analysis of temporal information across the entire recording. In this study, we present FUSE (Frame-Unified Stress Estimation), a facial-video stress detection framework that processes complete recordings as a single input without temporal windowing or external segmentation. The name reflects the defining operation of the method: rather than dividing a recording into short clips, all frames are fused into one unified two-dimensional representation from which the stress state is estimated. This unification is realized by folding the temporal dimension into the channel dimension of the spatial representation, and the resulting high-dimensional input is processed using a unified asymmetric-attention architecture. At a temporal stride of t = 1, FUSE retains the full 120-second recording as one input, corresponding to 3,600 frames at 30 fps. Experiments on a 58-subject stress dataset using a stratified subject-level protocol evaluate seven temporal-stride configurations, ranging from full-frame input to sparse subsampling. FUSE achieves the highest test accuracy of 69.44% at t = 15, while the full-frame configuration remains competitive at 69.03%. Across the stride range, computational cost varies from 12.48 to 348.78 GFLOPs, showing the trade-off between temporal density and efficiency. These results demonstrate that temporal windowing is not required for effective facial-video stress detection in this setting, and that complete-recording inference can be achieved within a single unified architecture.

AI.tldr: FUSE is a facial-video stress detection framework that processes complete video recordings as a single unified input without temporal windowing, by folding the temporal dimension into the channel dimension and using an asymmetric-attention architecture. It achieves 69.44% test accuracy on a 58-subject dataset, demonstrating that temporal windowing is not required for effective stress detection.
AI.motivation: Existing video-based stress detection approaches decompose recordings into short temporal windows, introducing design choices around window length, overlap, and aggregation while limiting direct analysis of temporal information across the full recording. The authors aim to eliminate this limitation by processing complete recordings as a single input.
AI.method: FUSE folds the temporal dimension into the channel dimension of the spatial representation, creating a unified 2D representation from all frames. The high-dimensional input is processed using a unified asymmetric-attention architecture. At a temporal stride of t=1, the full 120-second recording (3,600 frames at 30fps) is retained as one input.
AI.result: On a 58-subject stress dataset with stratified subject-level protocol, FUSE evaluated seven temporal-stride configurations. It achieved the highest test accuracy of 69.44% at t=15, with the full-frame configuration remaining competitive at 69.03%. Computational cost varied from 12.48 to 348.78 GFLOPs across the stride range.
AI.conclusion: Temporal windowing is not required for effective facial-video stress detection in this setting, and complete-recording inference can be achieved within a single unified architecture, offering a trade-off between temporal density and computational efficiency.

title: Bridging Event Streams and DiT: Event-Guided Video Frame Interpolation
summary: Latent diffusion models have recently advanced video frame interpolation by synthesizing intermediate frames between input images. However, handling large temporal gaps and complex motion remains challenging, often resulting in motion blur, structural distortions, and temporal inconsistencies. Event cameras provide high-temporal-resolution motion cues that are well suited for bridging these gaps and improving interpolation quality. To exploit this advantage without training an event-assisted model from scratch, we propose an adapter-based framework that incorporates event-derived cues into a pre-trained image-to-video diffusion model with minimal architectural changes. Specifically, our method leverages Image Warped Events (IWEs) and bidirectional sparse optical flow to provide spatially and temporally aligned guidance during generation. By injecting these event-guided structural and motion cues into the diffusion process, our approach reduces interpolation artifacts and improves both reconstruction fidelity and temporal coherence. Experimental results on real and synthetic benchmarks show that our method consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches. The project page is at https://joseph-lin-tech.github.io/BridgeEventDiT-VFI/.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes an adapter-based framework that incorporates event camera cues into a pre-trained image-to-video diffusion model for video frame interpolation, using Image Warped Events and bidirectional sparse optical flow to improve interpolation quality across large temporal gaps and complex motion.
AI.motivation: Latent diffusion models struggle with large temporal gaps and complex motion in video frame interpolation, leading to motion blur, structural distortions, and temporal inconsistencies. Event cameras offer high-temporal-resolution motion cues but typically require training an event-assisted model from scratch, which is expensive and limits adoption of powerful pre-trained models.
AI.method: The authors propose an adapter-based framework that injects event-derived cues (Image Warped Events and bidirectional sparse optical flow) into a pre-trained image-to-video diffusion model with minimal architectural changes. These event-guided structural and motion cues are used to provide spatially and temporally aligned guidance during the diffusion generation process.
AI.result: Experiments on real and synthetic benchmarks show the method consistently outperforms existing state-of-the-art approaches in video frame interpolation, reducing artifacts and improving reconstruction fidelity and temporal coherence.
AI.conclusion: Event-derived cues can be effectively integrated into pre-trained diffusion models via adapters, significantly improving video frame interpolation quality, particularly for large temporal gaps and complex motion, without requiring full retraining of the diffusion model.

title: When Vision Becomes Text: Visual Token Pruning via Cross-Modal Residual Guidance in VLMs
summary: Abundant visual information strengthens vision-language model (VLM) perception, yet massive visual tokens raise inference costs. Existing visual token pruning methods rely on similarity-based guidance, which exploits pairwise text-vision and vision-vision token correlations for compression. However, such methods only capture local layer-level signals and overlook the whole inference process in VLM. In this paper, we revisit VLM inference and present a new efficient guidance scheme that complements similarity-based guidance. In particular, we identify a key observation: as LLM layers deepen, text tokens continuously aggregate visual information via self-attention and progressively absorb partial visual content into textual representations. To quantify this phenomenon, we propose Cross Modal Absorption (CMA) from a geometric representation perspective to measure how much visual information is absorbed by text, revealing that more visual tokens in deeper layers can be approximately explained by the text subspace. We accordingly propose Cross Modal Residual (CMR). It projects visual tokens onto the text subspace via Tikhonov regularized least squares and exploits reconstruction residuals to quantify visual information that cannot be explained by text. Finally, based on CMR, we present SIEVE, a training-free visual token compression method that combines CMR, text-attention relevance, and residual-space diversity to retain task-relevant and complementary tokens. Experiments on diverse VLM architectures verify the effectiveness of SIEVE. For instance, on LLaVA-NeXT-7B, SIEVE keeps only $11.1\%$ of visual tokens while preserving $97.5\%$ of the original average performance, achieving $3.62\times$ prefill speedup, $2.49\times$ end-to-end speedup, and a $6.02\times$ KV-cache reduction.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes SIEVE, a training-free visual token compression method for vision-language models. It introduces Cross Modal Absorption (CMA) to measure how text tokens absorb visual information across layers, and Cross Modal Residual (CMR) to quantify visual information not explainable by text. SIEVE combines CMR, text-attention relevance, and residual-space diversity to prune visual tokens, achieving significant speedups and KV-cache reductions while preserving performance.
AI.motivation: Massive visual tokens in VLMs create high inference costs. Existing visual token pruning methods rely on similarity-based guidance that only captures local layer-level signals, overlooking the whole inference process in VLM. The paper identifies that text tokens progressively absorb visual information as LLM layers deepen, which can be leveraged for more effective compression.
AI.method: The paper proposes: (1) Cross Modal Absorption (CMA) to measure how much visual information is absorbed by text from a geometric representation perspective; (2) Cross Modal Residual (CMR) which projects visual tokens onto the text subspace via Tikhonov regularized least squares and uses reconstruction residuals to quantify unexplainable visual information; (3) SIEVE, a training-free compression method combining CMR, text-attention relevance, and residual-space diversity to retain task-relevant and complementary tokens.
AI.result: On LLaVA-NeXT-7B, SIEVE keeps only 11.1% of visual tokens while preserving 97.5% of original average performance, achieving 3.62x prefill speedup, 2.49x end-to-end speedup, and 6.02x KV-cache reduction. Experiments on diverse VLM architectures verify effectiveness.
AI.conclusion: SIEVE effectively complements similarity-based token pruning methods by exploiting the cross-modal absorption phenomenon throughout the inference process, providing a training-free solution that significantly reduces visual token counts and inference costs while maintaining high performance.

title: SapiensID 2.0: Aligning Human Recognition Foundation Models with Human Perception
summary: While foundation models have significantly advanced human recognition across diverse modalities, they predominantly rely on static, geometric feature extraction. This approach fundamentally diverges from human perception. Consequently, current models often suffer from "semantic blindness," overfitting to transient noise while failing to leverage invariant soft biometrics, and struggle to capture temporal motion signatures. To bridge this gap, we propose SapiensID 2.0, a human recognition framework enriched with both semantic and temporal awareness. To overcome the lack of soft-biometric annotations, we transfer zero-shot semantic knowledge from Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) into a discriminative embedding space. We resolve the dimensional mismatch between these spaces using Invariant Trait Alignment (ITA) to distill core persistent traits, and Transient Noise Disentanglement (TND) to decouple artifacts like clothing. Furthermore, we design a Kinematic Semantic Attention Head (K-SAH) that extends spatial attention across temporal windows. By tracking semantic patches over time, K-SAH captures rich kinematic signatures without requiring large-scale video datasets. Extensive experiments demonstrate that SapiensID 2.0 achieves state-of-the-art performance across image- and video-based person re-identification and gait recognition, while maintaining robust face recognition capabilities.

AI.tldr: SapiensID 2.0 is a human recognition framework that adds semantic and temporal awareness to overcome limitations of static geometric feature extraction. It transfers zero-shot semantic knowledge from MLLMs into a discriminative embedding space using Invariant Trait Alignment (ITA) and Transient Noise Disentanglement (TND), and introduces a Kinematic Semantic Attention Head (K-SAH) for temporal motion capture. It achieves SOTA results across person re-identification and gait recognition while maintaining face recognition robustness.
AI.motivation: Current foundation models for human recognition rely on static geometric features, diverging from human perception. This leads to "semantic blindness," overfitting to transient noise, and an inability to leverage invariant soft biometrics and temporal motion signatures.
AI.method: (1) Transfers zero-shot semantic knowledge from MLLMs into a discriminative embedding space; (2) Uses Invariant Trait Alignment (ITA) to distill core persistent traits despite dimensional mismatch; (3) Uses Transient Noise Disentanglement (TND) to decouple artifacts like clothing; (4) Designs a Kinematic Semantic Attention Head (K-SAH) extending spatial attention across temporal windows by tracking semantic patches over time.
AI.result: Achieves state-of-the-art performance across image- and video-based person re-identification and gait recognition, while maintaining robust face recognition capabilities.
AI.conclusion: SapiensID 2.0 demonstrates that injecting semantic (from MLLMs) and temporal (via K-SAH) awareness into human recognition frameworks bridges the gap between machine perception and human-like perception, improving robustness and performance without requiring large-scale video datasets.

title: DSAR: Dual-Stream Autoregressive Modeling of Temporal Cloth Dynamics for Photorealistic Animatable Avatars
comment: Accepted to ECCV 2026. 25 pages, 7 figures, including supplementary material
summary: Creating photorealistic and temporally coherent animatable human avatars from RGB videos remains challenging. Current methods struggle to capture realistic cloth dynamics, producing over-smoothed appearance or severe artifacts on out-of-distribution poses. This limitation stems from a fundamental oversight: existing approaches neglect the temporal causality inherent in cloth physics, where current states emerge from previous states through temporal evolution rather than instantaneous skeletal configurations alone. Without explicit modeling of this causal structure, networks learn pose-appearance correlations instead of motion evolution, leading to poor generalization. We introduce a dual-stream autoregressive framework that explicitly models both observable geometric information and implicit internal state. The geometric stream propagates surface displacement from the previous frame, while the state stream fuses current features with historical states retrieved from a memory bank. Motion-adaptive aggregation handles spatially-varying dynamics, and adaptive regularization balances smoothness with flexibility. Experiments on challenging datasets demonstrate significant improvements in rendering quality, temporal consistency, and generalization to motion patterns beyond training distributions, validating that dual-stream temporal modeling enables realistic cloth dynamics.

AI.tldr: A dual-stream autoregressive framework for animatable human avatars that explicitly models temporal causality in cloth physics, capturing realistic cloth dynamics from RGB videos with improved rendering quality, temporal consistency, and generalization to out-of-distribution poses.
AI.motivation: Current animatable avatar methods produce over-smoothed appearance and artifacts on out-of-distribution poses because they neglect temporal causality in cloth physics, learning pose-appearance correlations instead of motion evolution.
AI.method: Introduces a dual-stream autoregressive framework with: (1) a geometric stream propagating surface displacement from the previous frame, and (2) a state stream fusing current features with historical states from a memory bank. Motion-adaptive aggregation handles spatially-varying dynamics, and adaptive regularization balances smoothness with flexibility.
AI.result: Experiments on challenging datasets demonstrate significant improvements in rendering quality, temporal consistency, and generalization to motion patterns beyond training distributions.
AI.conclusion: Dual-stream temporal modeling that captures both observable geometry and implicit internal state enables realistic cloth dynamics for animatable avatars.

title: Towards Color-Faithful Low-Light Image Enhancement via Adaptive Color Debiasing and Saturation Rectification
summary: Low-light imaging often introduces color bias caused by the low signal-to-noise ratio and the image formation process. Although recent low-light image enhancement methods have achieved strong brightness recovery, faithful color restoration remains challenging, manifesting as overall color bias together with local under- and over-saturation. To address this issue, we propose CAGE, a cylindrical color correction framework with adaptive color debiasing and gamut-harmonized saturation rectification for color-faithful low-light image enhancement. We first introduce AdaLAB, a cylindrical adaptive LAB color space that provides a decoupled and image-specific basis for uniform color correction. Building on this color space, we further develop AdaCCT, an adaptive cylindrical color transform with forward and inverse transforms for the conversion between RGB and AdaLAB color space, as well as necessary color debiasing and saturation rectification. The forward transform suppresses embedded color bias before backbone enhancement by reorganizing the chromatic distribution through chromatic-plane shifting and scaling, while the inverse transform achieves faithful saturation rectification through out-of-gamut lightness compensation. Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks show that CAGE achieves more faithful color restoration, specifically reduces color bias and saturation abnormality, and delivers better overall visual quality across different low-light enhancement backbones. The code is available at https://yangzhichen763.github.io/CAGE/.

AI.tldr: CAGE is a cylindrical color correction framework for low-light image enhancement that addresses color bias via an adaptive LAB color space (AdaLAB) and adaptive cylindrical color transform (AdaCCT), achieving faithful color restoration and improved visual quality across benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Low-light imaging introduces color bias due to low signal-to-noise ratio and image formation. Existing enhancement methods recover brightness well but fail at faithful color restoration, showing overall color bias and local under/over-saturation.
AI.method: CAGE introduces AdaLAB, a cylindrical adaptive LAB color space for decoupled, image-specific color correction. It builds AdaCCT, an adaptive cylindrical color transform with forward and inverse transforms for RGB-AdaLAB conversion. The forward transform suppresses color bias via chromatic-plane shifting/scaling before backbone enhancement; the inverse transform performs saturation rectification via out-of-gamut lightness compensation.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on multiple benchmarks show CAGE achieves more faithful color restoration, reduces color bias and saturation abnormality, and delivers better overall visual quality across different low-light enhancement backbones.
AI.conclusion: CAGE provides a plug-and-play color correction framework that consistently improves color fidelity across various low-light enhancement backbones, with code publicly released.

title: SafeCap: Improving LVLM Safety with Image Captioning Reinforcement Learning
comment: 16pages, 4 figures. Preprint. Project page: https://safe-vlm.github.io/SafeCap/ ; code: https://github.com/Safe-VLM/SafeCap
summary: Large vision-language models (LVLMs) remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks that exploit visual inputs to bypass safety alignment inherited from their language backbones. We propose SafeCap, a reinforcement-learning framework that aligns LVLMs through learned self-captioning. SafeCap trains a policy model to first generate a safety-relevant image caption and then produce a final answer; the caption is further optimized by whether it enables a frozen LLM to reach a safety-aligned decision. This caption-mediated objective encourages the policy to expose visual cues relevant to safe response generation rather than relying solely on direct refusal supervision. Across five multimodal safety benchmarks and six vision-utility benchmarks, SafeCap substantially improves aggregate safety performance under its intended DirectCap protocol, with gains of 3.7-19.0 points in safety average across four model settings while maintaining comparable or improved vision utility. Under controlled comparisons on matched backbones and data, SafeCap outperforms safety SFT, DPO, and SafeGRPO, demonstrating the effectiveness of caption-mediated reinforcement learning for multimodal safety alignment.

AI.tldr: SafeCap is a reinforcement-learning framework for aligning large vision-language models (LVLMs) against jailbreak attacks via learned self-captioning. A policy model is trained to first generate a safety-relevant caption then a final answer, with the caption optimized based on whether it enables a frozen LLM to reach a safety-aligned decision. SafeCap improves safety performance by 3.7-19.0 points across benchmarks while maintaining vision utility, outperforming safety SFT, DPO, and SafeGRPO.
AI.motivation: Large vision-language models remain vulnerable to jailbreak attacks that exploit visual inputs to bypass safety alignment inherited from their language backbones. Existing safety alignment methods rely on direct refusal supervision, which may not effectively expose visual cues relevant to safe response generation.
AI.method: SafeCap trains a policy model via reinforcement learning to first generate a safety-relevant image caption and then produce a final answer. The caption is optimized by whether it enables a frozen LLM to reach a safety-aligned decision, using a caption-mediated objective that encourages exposing visual cues relevant to safe response generation rather than relying solely on direct refusal supervision.
AI.result: Across five multimodal safety benchmarks and six vision-utility benchmarks, SafeCap achieves 3.7-19.0 points improvement in safety average across four model settings under the DirectCap protocol while maintaining comparable or improved vision utility. Under controlled comparisons, SafeCap outperforms safety SFT, DPO, and SafeGRPO.
AI.conclusion: Caption-mediated reinforcement learning is an effective approach for multimodal safety alignment, demonstrating that learned self-captioning can enhance LVLM safety without sacrificing vision utility.

title: SparSTAR: Sparse Attention for SpaceTime AutoRegressive Video Synthesis
summary: InfinityStar extends visual autoregressive generation to video through a sequence of image and clip pyramids. Its changing scale and cross-clip context, however, leave late-scale attention costly and make sparse patterns reused from diffusion or image VAR models unreliable. We introduce SparSTAR, a training-free block-sparse attention method tailored to this setting. At each expensive scale and attention head, SparSTAR scores contiguous key blocks from the current query and key activations, retains required conditioning context, and executes the selected blocks through a forward-only sparse path. We analyze cross-scale consistency within a clip, pattern persistence across clip boundaries, and quality degradation as reuse spans increasingly distant scales. Across these analyses, important key blocks shift, showing that recomputing block selection at each target scale is more reliable than reusing a transferred mask. On 720p text-to-video and image-to-video generation, SparSTAR preserves every token and refinement scale while providing about a 1.6x end-to-end speedup and maintaining VBench and paired-output reconstruction fidelity close to dense InfinityStar.

AI.tldr: SparSTAR is a training-free block-sparse attention method for video autoregressive generation, extending visual AR to video via image and clip pyramids. It scores contiguous key blocks per scale/head, retains conditioning context, and uses forward-only sparse paths. It achieves ~1.6x end-to-end speedup on 720p text-to-video and image-to-video tasks while preserving VBench fidelity close to dense InfinityStar.
AI.motivation: InfinityStar's video autoregressive generation with changing scale and cross-clip context makes late-scale attention costly. Existing sparse patterns from diffusion or image VAR models are unreliable because important key blocks shift across scales and clip boundaries, so a tailored sparse attention approach is needed.
AI.method: SparSTAR performs training-free block-sparse attention. At each expensive scale and attention head, it scores contiguous key blocks from current query and key activations, retains required conditioning context, and executes selected blocks through a forward-only sparse path. It analyzes cross-scale consistency, pattern persistence across clip boundaries, and quality degradation over distant scale reuse.
AI.result: On 720p text-to-video and image-to-video generation, SparSTAR preserves all tokens and refinement scales with ~1.6x end-to-end speedup while maintaining VBench and paired-output reconstruction fidelity close to dense InfinityStar.
AI.conclusion: SparSTAR demonstrates that recomputing block selection at each target scale is more reliable than reusing transferred sparse masks, providing efficient sparse attention without training while maintaining generation quality in video autoregressive models.

title: Unlocking the Power of Medical Tabular Data via Semantic-Aware Multimodal Pre-training
comment: INTERNATIONAL CONFERENCE ON MEDICAL IMAGE COMPUTING AND COMPUTER ASSISTED INTERVENTION (ORAL presentation)
summary: While vision-language models dominate medical representation learning, unstructured text lacks the dense, quantitative diagnostic phenotypes inherent in structured clinical tables. However, existing multimodal pre-training methods underutilize this potential due to semantic-agnostic designs that treat tabular inputs as flat vectors and employ unstable continuous regression objectives. To overcome this, we propose a novel semantic-aware framework explicitly modeling the intrinsic two-dimensional structure of tabular data. First, addressing the inter-feature hierarchy of varying diagnostic importance, we introduce Importance-Aware Adaptive Masking to construct a label-free curriculum prioritizing salient features. Second, addressing the intra-feature continuity-discreteness duality, we propose a Soft-Label Discretized Module that replaces unstable numerical regression with stable distribution matching, thereby mathematically preserving ordinal relationships. Extensive experiments across large-scale dermatology (SLICE-3D, HOP) and ophthalmology (EyePACS) datasets establish a new state-of-the-art (SOTA), demonstrating exceptional robustness and cross-domain generalizability.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a semantic-aware multimodal framework for medical representation learning that explicitly models the two-dimensional structure of tabular clinical data, using Importance-Aware Adaptive Masking and a Soft-Label Discretized Module to achieve SOTA performance on dermatology and ophthalmology datasets.
AI.motivation: Existing multimodal pre-training methods for medical vision-language models underutilize structured clinical tables because they treat tabular inputs as flat vectors (ignoring inter-feature hierarchy) and employ unstable continuous regression objectives (ignoring intra-feature continuity-discreteness duality).
AI.method: The framework introduces two key components: (1) Importance-Aware Adaptive Masking, which constructs a label-free curriculum prioritizing salient features to address varying diagnostic importance across features; and (2) a Soft-Label Discretized Module that replaces unstable numerical regression with stable distribution matching, preserving ordinal relationships mathematically.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on large-scale dermatology datasets (SLICE-3D, HOP) and ophthalmology dataset (EyePACS) establish a new state-of-the-art, demonstrating exceptional robustness and cross-domain generalizability.
AI.conclusion: The semantic-aware modeling of tabular structure significantly improves multimodal medical learning, setting new SOTA performance while being robust and generalizable across different medical domains.

title: Rethinking Text-Based Image Retrieval in Specific Domain
summary: Driven by the rapid advancement of vision-language representation learning, Text-based Image Retrieval (TBIR) has made notable progress. However, existing benchmarks are predominantly constructed on an exclusive single-match assumption between query and images. While effective in general scenarios, this assumption fails to reflect practical system performance in specific domains (e.g., surveillance), where a single query often corresponds to multiple relevant candidate images. To address this limitation, we design a Domain-Specific Multi-Match Text-based Image Retrieval (DSMM-TBIR) data engine. Leveraging this engine, we construct Security Multi-Match TBIR (SecMM-TBIR), a benchmark comprising 50k surveillance images with 200 comprehensive queries. Furthermore, we observe that vanilla contrastive learning in specific domains suffers from severe false negatives, forcing the model to push apart semantically similar pairs and thus degrading retrieval performance. We propose the Semantic-Aware Fine-Tuning (SAFT) framework to address semantic compression in specific domains, which incorporates Semantic-Aware Soft-Label Supervision (SASS) and Intra-modal Structural Distillation (ISD) to establish a promising paradigm for domain-specific TBIR tasks. Experiments across diverse CLIP-like models demonstrate that SAFT yields an average mAP@20 gain of 7.8 points on SecMM-TBIR over standard image-text contrastive (ITC) fine-tuning, while also improving general-domain performance. The entire benchmark will be released to facilitate further research.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces DSMM-TBIR, a data engine for Domain-Specific Multi-Match Text-based Image Retrieval, and constructs SecMM-TBIR, a surveillance benchmark with 50k images and 200 queries. To address false negatives from vanilla contrastive learning in multi-match settings, the authors propose SAFT (Semantic-Aware Fine-Tuning) with SASS and ISD, achieving an average mAP@20 gain of 7.8 points over standard ITC fine-tuning.
AI.motivation: Existing TBIR benchmarks rely on an exclusive single-match assumption between query and image, which fails to reflect real-world performance in domains like surveillance where one query can match multiple relevant images.
AI.method: Designs a Domain-Specific Multi-Match Text-based Image Retrieval (DSMM-TBIR) data engine to construct the SecMM-TBIR benchmark. Proposes SAFT framework incorporating Semantic-Aware Soft-Label Supervision (SASS) and Intra-modal Structural Distillation (ISD) to mitigate false negatives and semantic compression.
AI.result: SAFT achieves an average mAP@20 gain of 7.8 points on SecMM-TBIR over standard image-text contrastive fine-tuning across diverse CLIP-like models, while also improving general-domain performance.
AI.conclusion: The proposed benchmark and framework establish a promising paradigm for domain-specific TBIR tasks, and the benchmark will be released to facilitate further research.

title: Dynamic Context Adapters: Efficiently Infusing History into Vision-and-Language Models
summary: Historical context integration presents a fundamental challenge for Vision-Language Models (VLMs) in sequential decision-making tasks. Current VLMs process visual inputs independently, which creates critical limitations for downstream applications that require temporal understanding. Direct incorporation of historical frames into Transformer inputs produces quadratic attention complexity and excessive memory consumption. Existing approaches suffer from significant drawbacks: computational inflation or substantial information loss through temporal compression. To address these challenges, we introduce Dynamic Context Adapter (DCA), a novel context injection approach for pretrained VLMs. Our method employs fixed-size, dynamically compressed memory to preserve historical semantics without frame concatenation. DCA bridges static VLMs and recurrent policies and enables memory capabilities in pretrained models while maintaining computational efficiency. DCA achieves over $25\%$ reduction in attention FLOPs and $13\%$ memory savings while improving performance on long-horizon tasks.

AI.tldr: Introduces Dynamic Context Adapter (DCA), a context injection method for pretrained VLMs in sequential decision-making that uses fixed-size dynamically compressed memory to preserve historical semantics without frame concatenation, achieving over 25% reduction in attention FLOPs and 13% memory savings while improving performance on long-horizon tasks.
AI.motivation: Current VLMs process visual inputs independently, lacking temporal understanding needed for sequential decision-making. Direct historical frame incorporation causes quadratic attention complexity and excessive memory, while existing approaches suffer from either computational inflation or substantial information loss through temporal compression.
AI.method: Dynamic Context Adapter (DCA) employs fixed-size, dynamically compressed memory to preserve historical semantics without frame concatenation, bridging static VLMs and recurrent policies to enable memory capabilities in pretrained models while maintaining computational efficiency.
AI.result: DCA achieves over 25% reduction in attention FLOPs and 13% memory savings while improving performance on long-horizon tasks.
AI.conclusion: DCA provides an efficient solution for integrating historical context into VLMs for sequential decision-making, avoiding the trade-offs of computational inflation and information loss seen in existing approaches.

title: Flow Straight to Reality: Perceptually Consistent Flow Matching for Efficient Image Restoration
comment: Accepted to ECCV 2026. Code is available at https://github.com/aiimaginglab/PCFlow
summary: Image restoration is fundamentally constrained by the tradeoff between distortion and perception: minimizing pixel-wise error yields over-smoothed results, whereas optimizing for perceptual realism often introduces structural deviations. Recent approaches attempt to balance this tradeoff via posterior sampling or multi-stage generative pipelines, yet remain computationally expensive and architecturally complex. To overcome these limitations, we propose PCFlow (Perceptually Consistent Flow Matching), a unified framework that directly parameterizes a continuous transport from degraded observations to clean targets, jointly optimizing distortion and perceptual quality. While its latent consistency flow objective drives stable and efficient few-step inference, a Latent Consistency Perceptual Loss (LCPL) imposes semantic constraints directly on the guiding velocity field, steering the dynamics toward visually sharp data manifolds. Furthermore, recognizing the inherent conflict between structural and perceptual consistencies, we integrate a conflict-free gradient projection strategy to stabilize the multi-objective optimization landscape. Combined with lightweight, convolution-only backbone, PCFlow achieves competitive performance across diverse restoration tasks at a fraction of traditional computational costs.

AI.tldr: PCFlow is a unified flow-matching framework that directly parameterizes continuous transport from degraded to clean images, jointly optimizing distortion and perceptual quality via a latent consistency flow objective, a Latent Consistency Perceptual Loss (LCPL) on the velocity field, and a conflict-free gradient projection strategy, achieving competitive restoration performance with lightweight convolution-only backbones at low computational cost.
AI.motivation: Image restoration faces a fundamental tradeoff between distortion (pixel-wise accuracy) and perception (visual realism). Existing approaches using posterior sampling or multi-stage generative pipelines are computationally expensive and architecturally complex, motivating a simpler unified framework.
AI.method: PCFlow proposes a unified flow-matching framework that (1) parameterizes a continuous transport from degraded observations to clean targets, (2) uses a latent consistency flow objective for stable few-step inference, (3) applies a Latent Consistency Perceptual Loss (LCPL) to impose semantic constraints on the guiding velocity field, and (4) integrates a conflict-free gradient projection strategy to stabilize multi-objective optimization, all with a lightweight convolution-only backbone.
AI.result: PCFlow achieves competitive performance across diverse restoration tasks while requiring only a fraction of traditional computational costs.
AI.conclusion: PCFlow demonstrates that direct transport parameterization with consistency flow and perceptual constraints on velocity fields can effectively balance distortion and perception tradeoffs without complex multi-stage architectures, offering an efficient unified solution for image restoration.

title: A HamNoSys-Guided Dataset and Baselines for Fine-Grained Isolated Handshape Recognition in Sign Language
summary: Purpose: Fine-grained handshape recognition supports computational sign-language transcription, recognition, and translation, but broad, phonetically defined visual inventories with signer-aware evaluation remain limited. This work introduces a benchmark grounded in the language-independent Hamburg Notation System (HamNoSys). Methods: A balanced dataset of 144,000 RGB images was collected from 15 participants for 160 handshape classes defined by the official HamNoSys 4 Handshapes Chart. ResNet-18 and ViT-B/16 were evaluated as appearance-based models, while a graph convolutional network and XGBoost were evaluated from hand landmarks. Both a class-stratified subject-dependent split and a 15-fold leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) protocol were used. The same model families were additionally assessed on LSWH100 and ASL Fingerspelling Dataset A for external context. Results: The subject-dependent benchmarks established reproducible reference performance across all four model families, whereas LOSO evaluation exposed a substantial reduction when recognition was required to generalise to unseen participants. On ASL Fingerspelling Dataset A, mean LOSO top-1 accuracy ranged from 82.20% to 87.40%. Conclusion: The documented acquisition, curation, and complementary evaluation protocols pro-vide a reproducible resource for fine-grained isolated-handshape research and for developing more accessible sign-language technologies.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a benchmark for fine-grained handshape recognition based on the Hamburg Notation System (HamNoSys), with a balanced dataset of 144,000 RGB images from 15 participants covering 160 handshape classes. Four model families (ResNet-18, ViT-B/16, GCN, XGBoost) are evaluated under subject-dependent and leave-one-subject-out protocols, with external validation on LSWH100 and ASL Fingerspelling Dataset A.
AI.motivation: Fine-grained handshape recognition is important for sign-language transcription, recognition, and translation, but broad phonetically defined visual inventories with signer-aware evaluation remain limited. This work addresses this gap by introducing a benchmark grounded in the language-independent HamNoSys notation.
AI.method: A balanced dataset of 144,000 RGB images was collected from 15 participants for 160 handshape classes from the official HamNoSys 4 Handshapes Chart. Appearance-based models (ResNet-18, ViT-B/16) and landmark-based models (GCN, XGBoost) were evaluated using both class-stratified subject-dependent splits and 15-fold leave-one-subject-out (LOSO) protocols. The same model families were also assessed on LSWH100 and ASL Fingerspelling Dataset A.
AI.result: Subject-dependent benchmarks established reproducible reference performance across all four model families, while LOSO evaluation revealed substantial performance reduction when generalizing to unseen participants. On ASL Fingerspelling Dataset A, mean LOSO top-1 accuracy ranged from 82.20% to 87.40%.
AI.conclusion: The documented acquisition, curation, and complementary evaluation protocols provide a reproducible resource for fine-grained isolated-handshape research and for developing more accessible sign-language technologies.

title: $π$-SUB: A Physics-Informed Synthetic Underwater Benchmark Dataset for Underwater Image Enhancement
summary: This paper presents $π$-SUB, a physics-informed framework for generating synthetic underwater benchmark datasets that bridges the synthetic-to-real gap for Underwater Image Enhancement (UIE). The proposed framework extends the classical underwater image formation model by incorporating depth-dependent downwelling irradiance, biologically resolved absorption, and environmental scattering across all ten Jerlov water types, together with independently controllable residual phenomena. Using this framework, the $π$-SUB dataset consists of paired synthetic underwater-reference images spanning shallow-to-deep and coastal-to-oceanic environments. Extensive simulation studies have been carried out to evaluate $π$-SUB along two criteria namely hyper-realism and generalizability. For hyper-realism, $π$-SUB attains a global Frechet Inception Distance (FID) that is 46% lower than Syrea. For generalizability, four state-of-the-art UIE architectures (FUnIE-GAN, Pix2Pix, PUIE-Net, and Phaseformer) are used for comparative evaluation of $π$-SUB. These models were independently trained on six datasets including one real and five synthetic datasets and tested on six real-world benchmarks datasets. Across four UIE architectures and six real benchmark datasets, $π$-SUB improves UIQM by 4.18% over PHISWID (next best) and 9.46% over Syrea (next best), while reducing NIQE by 48.78% and 23.98%, respectively. These results establish $π$-SUB as a hyper-realistic and generalizable benchmark for developing the next generation of underwater image enhancement methods. The code and dataset are available at https://github.com/airl-iisc/pi-SUB

AI.tldr: π-SUB is a physics-informed framework that generates synthetic underwater benchmark datasets for Underwater Image Enhancement (UIE), extending classical image formation models with depth-dependent irradiance, biologically resolved absorption, and environmental scattering across all ten Jerlov water types. It achieves 46% lower FID than Syrea and improves UIQM by up to 9.46% while reducing NIQE by up to 48.78% across four UIE architectures and six real benchmark datasets.
AI.motivation: There is a significant synthetic-to-real gap in Underwater Image Enhancement (UIE) research, where existing synthetic datasets fail to realistically represent underwater imaging conditions, limiting the generalizability of trained models to real-world scenarios.
AI.method: π-SUB extends the classical underwater image formation model by incorporating depth-dependent downwelling irradiance, biologically resolved absorption, and environmental scattering across all ten Jerlov water types, along with independently controllable residual phenomena. The framework generates paired synthetic underwater-reference images covering shallow-to-deep and coastal-to-oceanic environments.
AI.result: π-SUB achieves a global FID 46% lower than Syrea for hyper-realism. Across four UIE architectures (FUnIE-GAN, Pix2Pix, PUIE-Net, Phaseformer) and six real benchmark datasets, π-SUB improves UIQM by 4.18% over PHISWID and 9.46% over Syrea, while reducing NIQE by 48.78% and 23.98%, respectively.
AI.conclusion: π-SUB is established as a hyper-realistic and generalizable benchmark for developing next-generation underwater image enhancement methods, with code and dataset publicly available.

title: Rethinking Data Efficiency in Industrial Dense Prediction: Pretraining Coherence, Not Inductive Bias, Determines ViTs Low-Data Advantage
comment: 14 pages, 10 figures, 17 tables. This paper targets industrial defect detection via vision transformer and CNN alignment grafting
summary: Vision Transformers (ViTs) are widely believed to require more labeled data than CNNs for industrial dense prediction. Through controlled experiments on four industrial datasets, we show that the data-efficiency gap stems from pretraining incoherence, which refers to the statistical mismatch between ImageNet-pretrained ViT backbones and COCO-pretrained CNN necks, rather than from inherent self-attention deficits. We characterize the cross-architecture feature gap and propose a lightweight AlignBlock family for pyramid-level feature recalibration. Our core finding empirically identifies a data-efficiency frontier: for domain-proximal scenes with >= 200 samples, Swin-Graft surpasses YOLOv11x (terminal 703-shot: 0.973 vs 0.956 mAP@50); for domain-distant scenes, CNNs retain advantage (hook 141-shot: 0.900 vs 0.600 mAP@50). Grafted neck weights yield up to 2.5x the mAP of a randomly initialized neck.

AI.tldr: This paper challenges the assumption that Vision Transformers (ViTs) require more labeled data than CNNs for dense prediction tasks. Through controlled experiments on four industrial datasets, the authors show that ViTs' apparent data inefficiency stems from pretraining incoherence—a statistical mismatch between ImageNet-pretrained ViT backbones and COCO-pretrained CNN necks—rather than inherent self-attention limitations. They propose a lightweight AlignBlock family for feature recalibration and identify a data-efficiency frontier: Swin-Graft surpasses YOLOv11x on domain-proximal scenes with ≥200 samples, while CNNs retain the advantage on domain-distant scenes. Grafted neck weights yield up to 2.5x the mAP of randomly initialized necks.
AI.motivation: The paper aims to investigate and explain why Vision Transformers are perceived as data-hungry compared to CNNs in industrial dense prediction tasks, and to determine whether this gap is inherent to the architecture or caused by external factors such as pretraining strategy mismatches.
AI.method: The authors conduct controlled experiments on four industrial datasets comparing ViT-based and CNN-based models. They identify and characterize a cross-architecture feature gap (pretraining incoherence) between ImageNet-pretrained ViT backbones and COCO-pretrained CNN necks, and propose a lightweight AlignBlock family for pyramid-level feature recalibration to bridge this gap.
AI.result: The paper reveals a data-efficiency frontier: for domain-proximal scenes with ≥200 samples, Swin-Graft outperforms YOLOv11x (0.973 vs 0.956 mAP@50 at 703 shots); for domain-distant scenes, CNNs retain superiority (0.900 vs 0.600 at 141 shots). Grafted neck weights achieve up to 2.5x the mAP of a randomly initialized neck, demonstrating that the bottleneck is pretraining incoherence, not the ViT architecture itself.
AI.conclusion: ViTs' apparent data inefficiency in dense prediction is primarily caused by pretraining incoherence between heterogeneous backbone and neck components, which can be mitigated with lightweight feature recalibration (AlignBlock). The choice between ViT and CNN architectures should depend on domain proximity and available sample size, as captured by the identified data-efficiency frontier.

title: Gaussian Sculpting: End-to-End Controllable Surface Reconstruction via Field Optimization
summary: 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS) has recently enabled real-time novel view synthesis with impressive quality. However, it struggles to recover accurate surfaces under limited viewpoints and due to the inherent irregularity of Gaussian primitives. The resulting geometric errors are notoriously difficult to correct manually. To address these issues, we propose Gaussian Sculpting, a fully differentiable end-to-end framework for high-quality surface reconstruction. Our key insight is to anchor Gaussians onto an evolving differentiable surface, allowing them to guide signed distance field (SDF) optimization instead of extracting the surface only during post-processing. To enable stable gradient isolation during joint optimization, we design a bi-level training strategy in which the outer loop optimizes the geometry represented by the SDF, while the inner loop updates the Gaussians with the geometry fixed. We further impose constraints on Gaussian parameters to ensure consistency with the underlying surface, thereby improving both geometric and appearance fidelity during optimization. In addition, we introduce a multi-resolution subdivision scheme based on octree-like partitioning to preserve fine details while reducing memory consumption. Experiments on object-level scenes demonstrate that our method effectively removes redundant surfaces, recovers missing structures caused by limited viewpoints, and achieves strong reconstruction quality even at relatively low resolutions.

AI.tldr: Gaussian Sculpting is a fully differentiable end-to-end framework for high-quality surface reconstruction that anchors 3D Gaussians onto an evolving differentiable surface, using a bi-level training strategy (outer loop optimizes SDF geometry, inner loop updates Gaussians) and an octree-like multi-resolution subdivision scheme to improve geometric accuracy and appearance fidelity.
AI.motivation: 3D Gaussian Splatting enables real-time novel view synthesis but struggles to recover accurate surfaces under limited viewpoints due to the inherent irregularity of Gaussian primitives. The resulting geometric errors are difficult to correct manually, necessitating a more robust surface reconstruction approach.
AI.method: The framework anchors Gaussians onto an evolving differentiable surface, guiding SDF optimization throughout the process rather than extracting surfaces only during post-processing. It employs a bi-level training strategy (outer loop for SDF geometry, inner loop for Gaussians with fixed geometry) for stable gradient isolation, imposes constraints on Gaussian parameters for surface consistency, and introduces an octree-like multi-resolution subdivision scheme to preserve details while reducing memory usage.
AI.result: Experiments on object-level scenes show the method effectively removes redundant surfaces, recovers missing structures caused by limited viewpoints, and achieves strong reconstruction quality even at relatively low resolutions.
AI.conclusion: The proposed bi-level optimization approach successfully couples Gaussian Splatting with SDF-based surface reconstruction, demonstrating improved geometric fidelity and robustness under challenging conditions such as limited viewpoints and low resolution.

title: InSight-doc: Agentic Visual Perception for Long-Document Understanding
summary: Long-document understanding often requires reasoning over many visually rich pages, making inference costly and prone to context rot. In this work, we propose InSight-doc, an agentic visual perception framework that treats visual resolution as an adaptive reasoning-time resource. InSight-doc starts from low resolution and selectively zooms into high-resolution regions for finer evidence, without relying on any external retriever. To train such an agent, we construct an active-perception corpus of 17.9K high-quality SFT examples with region-level zoom-in trajectories, accompanied by 19.2K hard RL examples. Through SFT+RL, InSight-doc-8B improves the baseline by 4.3--16.4 accuracy points over document VQA benchmarks. On long documents, it reduces hallucination by more than 40% and inference latency by 41%--68% while maintaining an accuracy lead. Our code, datasets, and model are released at https://github.com/m-Just/InSight-doc .

AI.tldr: InSight-doc is an agentic visual perception framework for long-document understanding that treats visual resolution as an adaptive reasoning-time resource, starting from low resolution and selectively zooming into high-resolution regions without external retrievers. Trained via SFT+RL on 17.9K SFT examples and 19.2K hard RL examples, InSight-doc-8B improves accuracy by 4.3–16.4 points on document VQA benchmarks, reduces hallucination by over 40% on long documents, and cuts inference latency by 41%–68% while maintaining accuracy gains.
AI.motivation: Long-document understanding requires reasoning over many visually rich pages, which makes inference costly and prone to context rot. Existing methods lack an efficient way to allocate visual resolution adaptively during reasoning.
AI.method: The framework operates as an agent that starts from low resolution and selectively zooms into high-resolution regions for finer evidence, requiring no external retriever. Training uses an active-perception corpus with 17.9K high-quality SFT examples featuring region-level zoom-in trajectories plus 19.2K hard RL examples, trained via SFT followed by RL.
AI.result: InSight-doc-8B improves baseline by 4.3–16.4 accuracy points across document VQA benchmarks. On long documents, it reduces hallucination by more than 40% and inference latency by 41%–68%, while still maintaining an accuracy lead.
AI.conclusion: Adaptive resolution allocation through an agentic zoom-in mechanism is an effective and efficient strategy for long-document visual understanding, and the resources (code, datasets, model) are publicly released.

title: MedUP: Awakening Unified Understanding and Perception in Medical Vision-Language Models
summary: Medical Vision-Language Models (Med-VLMs) excel at verbalizing visual content, yet precise visual perception, segmentation, and grounding remain challenging. Existing approaches either verbalize regions as coordinate strings or rely on external modules that decouple perception from understanding, creating representation gaps for region-language alignment. We present MedUP, a Med-VLM that natively unifies perception and understanding within a shared token space. At its core lies UniMedTok, a region tokenizer that encodes masks as discrete tokens in the LLM vocabulary, enabling the model to seamlessly interleave mask tokens with text. We curate UniMed-Train, a 1.84M-instance corpus spanning text-guided segmentation, region-grounded understanding, medical VQA and CoT-based segmentation, and introduce UniMed-Bench for unified evaluation. Extensive experiments show that MedUP outperforms native, agentic, and dual-decoder Med-VLMs across all tasks while remaining competitive with specialist segmentors, demonstrating the strong potential of unified understanding and perception modeling.

AI.tldr: MedUP is a Medical Vision-Language Model that natively unifies perception and understanding within a shared token space via UniMedTok, a region tokenizer encoding masks as discrete LLM vocabulary tokens. It is trained on UniMed-Train (1.84M instances) and evaluated on UniMed-Bench, outperforming native, agentic, and dual-decoder Med-VLMs across all tasks while staying competitive with specialist segmentors.
AI.motivation: Existing Med-VLMs struggle with precise visual perception, segmentation, and grounding because they either verbalize regions as coordinate strings or rely on external modules that decouple perception from understanding, creating representation gaps for region-language alignment.
AI.method: MedUP introduces UniMedTok, a region tokenizer that encodes masks as discrete tokens in the LLM vocabulary, enabling seamless interleaving of mask tokens with text. The model is trained on a curated 1.84M-instance corpus (UniMed-Train) covering text-guided segmentation, region-grounded understanding, medical VQA, and CoT-based segmentation, with evaluation on the unified UniMed-Bench benchmark.
AI.result: MedUP outperforms native, agentic, and dual-decoder Med-VLMs across all evaluated tasks and remains competitive with specialist segmentation models.
AI.conclusion: The strong performance of MedUP demonstrates the potential of unified understanding and perception modeling in the medical vision-language domain, achieved by sharing a single token space for both language and visual masks.

title: Precise Top-Layer Fabric Segmentation for Fabric Destacking with Edge- and Shape-Aware Deep Networks
comment: 7 pages, 3 figures. Published in IEEE ICMA 2025. Author's accepted manuscript. Code: https://github.com/bhattner143/top-layer-fab-seg
summary: Fabric destacking requires precise segmentation of the topmost fabric layer, a task complicated by subtle fabric boundaries and high visual similarity between fabric layers. Existing semantic and edge-based segmentation approaches often struggle with these complexities, limiting the performance of robotic manipulation for different tasks. In this work, a novel segmentation training architecture tailored for top-layer fabric segmentation in stacked fabrics is proposed. The method extends the classical encoder-decoder framework by introducing two specialized branches - an edge-aware branch and a shape-aware branch - that are used to supervise the backbone network for better tuning. The edge-aware branch enhances boundary delineation, while the shape-aware branch guides the network to capture and align the overall fabric shape with reference masks derived from Computer Aided Design (CAD) models. Experiments on a real-world fabric dataset demonstrate that the training approach outperforms established baselines, verifying the effectiveness of the multi-branch design through both quantitative results and ablation studies.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a novel segmentation training architecture for top-layer fabric segmentation in stacked fabrics, extending the encoder-decoder framework with two specialized branches (edge-aware and shape-aware) to improve boundary delineation and shape alignment using CAD reference masks.
AI.motivation: Fabric destacking requires precise segmentation of the topmost fabric layer, but existing semantic and edge-based segmentation approaches struggle with subtle fabric boundaries and high visual similarity between fabric layers, limiting robotic manipulation performance.
AI.method: The method extends the classical encoder-decoder framework by introducing two specialized branches: an edge-aware branch for enhanced boundary delineation and a shape-aware branch that guides the network to capture and align overall fabric shape with reference masks derived from CAD models. These branches supervise the backbone network for better tuning.
AI.result: Experiments on a real-world fabric dataset show the training approach outperforms established baselines, with quantitative results and ablation studies verifying the effectiveness of the multi-branch design.
AI.conclusion: The multi-branch training architecture effectively addresses the challenges of top-layer fabric segmentation in stacked fabrics, improving segmentation quality through edge-aware and shape-aware supervision.

title: PolypVision: A Three-Stage Hierarchical Deep Learning Framework for Classification and Segmentation of Colorectal Polyps
summary: Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide, predominantly arising from precancerous polyps. Accurate detection, segmentation, and endoscopic and histological classification of colorectal polyps are crucial for timely clinical intervention. In this study, we present PolypVision, a three-stage hierarchical deep learning framework that sequentially performs: (Stage 1) binary classification of polyps as adenomatous or hyperplastic, with simultaneous Paris and JNet classification, using EfficientNetV2-M with Focal Loss; (Stage 2) polyp segmentation with recommended resection method using a UNet++ decoder with the Stage 1 backbone as encoder, optimized with Dice and BCE losses; and (Stage 3) adenoma subtype classification (tubular, tubulovillous, villous) using EfficientNetV2-M with transfer learning from Stage 2. Evaluated on three public datasets -- PolypGen, Kvasir-SEG, and CVC-ClinicDB -- PolypVision achieves an AUC of approximately 0.99 for frame classification and a detection mAP@50 of 94.4% on Kvasir-SEG, outperforming or matching state-of-the-art methods. Gradient-weighted Class Activation Maps (Grad-CAM) confirm that the model attends to clinically relevant lesion features. The framework is device-independent, operating across diverse endoscopic imaging systems without hardware-specific adaptation. These results demonstrate that a hierarchical, transfer-learning-driven pipeline with task-specific loss functions offers a robust, device-independent, and clinically meaningful approach to automated colorectal polyp analysis. PolypVision is freely available as a web application at https://polypvision.com, a DataBioX initiative, with a free usage tier open to all users.

AI.tldr: PolypVision is a three-stage hierarchical deep learning framework for automated colorectal polyp analysis, performing binary classification (adenomatous vs. hyperplastic), segmentation with resection recommendation, and adenoma subtype classification. It achieves ~0.99 AUC and 94.4% mAP@50, is device-independent, and is available as a free web application.
AI.motivation: Colorectal cancer is a leading cause of cancer mortality, and accurate detection, segmentation, and classification of colorectal polyps are critical for timely intervention but remain challenging across diverse endoscopic systems.
AI.method: A three-stage hierarchical framework: (1) EfficientNetV2-M with Focal Loss for binary polyp classification plus Paris and JNet classification; (2) UNet++ decoder with Stage 1 backbone for segmentation and resection method recommendation, using Dice and BCE losses; (3) EfficientNetV2-M with transfer learning from Stage 2 for adenoma subtype classification.
AI.result: On PolypGen, Kvasir-SEG, and CVC-ClinicDB, PolypVision achieves ~0.99 AUC for frame classification and 94.4% detection mAP@50 on Kvasir-SEG, outperforming or matching state-of-the-art. Grad-CAM confirms attention to clinically relevant lesion features.
AI.conclusion: A hierarchical, transfer-learning-driven pipeline with task-specific loss functions provides a robust, device-independent, and clinically meaningful approach to automated colorectal polyp analysis, freely available as a web application.

title: Cross-View Sequential Visual Localization with Spatio-Temporal Context Modeling for Autonomous Driving
summary: Continuous and reliable localization is essential for autonomous driving. Cross-view visual localization matches ground images with satellite maps, providing complementary localization cues for pipelines that depend on Global Navigation Satellite System (GNSS) signals and high-definition (HD) maps. Most existing cross-view visual localization methods process each frame independently, leaving temporal information underused and limiting accuracy under dynamic occlusion, illumination variation, and repetitive textures. This study proposes a temporal-context-enhanced framework for cross-view sequence visual localization. The proposed recurrent cross-frame module aggregates historical context from the previous state to enhance the coarse ground feature of each current frame. These enhanced features facilitate satellite candidate-region classification, while hierarchical fine-grained features enable precise local offset estimation. On the CVIS dataset, the proposed method reduces mean localization error from 3.80 m to 1.57 m and increases R@1 m from 8.14% to 40.22%. Direct transfer to KITTI-CVL achieves a mean error of 2.61 m, with target-domain fine-tuning further reducing the mean error to 2.27 m. Zero-shot field experiments on a real-world vehicle achieve a mean error of 2.84 m and R@5 m of 96.86%. These results demonstrate that temporal context enhancement significantly improves cross-view localization accuracy and supports robust deployment on public benchmarks and real-world roads.

AI.tldr: This paper proposes a temporal-context-enhanced framework for cross-view sequence visual localization that aggregates historical context from previous frames via a recurrent cross-frame module, reducing mean localization error from 3.80m to 1.57m on CVIS and achieving robust real-world performance with 96.86% R@5m.
AI.motivation: Existing cross-view visual localization methods process each frame independently, leaving temporal information underused and limiting accuracy under dynamic occlusion, illumination variation, and repetitive textures in autonomous driving scenarios.
AI.method: The framework uses a recurrent cross-frame module to aggregate historical context from previous states, enhancing coarse ground features for each current frame. Enhanced features enable satellite candidate-region classification, while hierarchical fine-grained features provide precise local offset estimation.
AI.result: On CVIS dataset, mean localization error reduced from 3.80m to 1.57m and R@1m increased from 8.14% to 40.22%. Direct transfer to KITTI-CVL achieves 2.61m mean error, fine-tuning reduces it to 2.27m. Zero-shot real-world experiments achieve 2.84m mean error and 96.86% R@5m.
AI.conclusion: Temporal context enhancement significantly improves cross-view localization accuracy and supports robust deployment on both public benchmarks and real-world roads.

title: Chartography: A Benchmark for Professional Chart Understanding
comment: 16 pages, 5 figures, 5 tables. Accepted at the 2nd Workshop on Benchmarking Evidence-Aligned Multimodal Reasoning (BEAM 2), ECCV 2026
summary: Professionals across medicine, engineering, finance, manufacturing, and the sciences often make consequential decisions from charts. Existing chart benchmarks do not sufficiently measure this ability: they are dominated by bar, line, and pie formats, rely on shorter reasoning chains, and are nearing saturation, with frontier models already scoring 80-90%. We introduce Chartography, a benchmark of 100 tasks that pair charts drawn from professional practice, in domain-specific formats that standard chart benchmarks rarely include, with questions written by professionals who read these charts for a living and independently verified by three additional experts. In an evaluation of 30 frontier-model configurations (20 scored trials per task), the best configuration reaches only 45.0% mean pass@1; the remainder span 9.0-39.5%. Failures concentrate in visual perception: models can miss nuanced features, misread values along sparsely labeled axes, mishandle projected 3D geometry, and violate domain conventions encoded in the chart. We release all tasks, images, provenance metadata, and evaluation code.

AI.tldr: Chartography is a new benchmark of 100 chart-reading tasks drawn from professional practice, featuring domain-specific chart formats not found in standard benchmarks.
