When evaluated across 30 frontier-model configurations, the best configuration achieves only 45.0% mean pass@1, revealing that current models significantly underperform on professional-grade chart interpretation, with failures concentrated in visual perception.
AI.motivation: Existing chart benchmarks fail to adequately measure professional chart-reading ability because they are dominated by simple bar, line, and pie formats, rely on shorter reasoning chains, and are approaching saturation with frontier models already scoring 80-90%. This leaves a gap in evaluating models on the complex, domain-specific charts professionals actually use for consequential decision-making.
AI.method: The authors introduce Chartography, a benchmark of 100 tasks pairing charts from professional practice (in domain-specific formats rarely included in standard benchmarks) with questions written by professionals who read these charts for a living, with each question independently verified by three additional experts. They evaluate 30 frontier-model configurations with 20 scored trials per task.
AI.result: The best model configuration reaches only 45.0% mean pass@1, while the remainder score between 9.0-39.5%. Failures concentrate in visual perception: models miss nuanced features, misread values along sparsely labeled axes, mishandle projected 3D geometry, and violate domain conventions encoded in charts.
AI.conclusion: Chartography reveals that frontier models remain far from achieving expert-level chart comprehension in professional domains. The benchmark exposes a significant gap between model performance on simple chart benchmarks (80-90%) and professional chart-reading tasks (45% at best), highlighting visual perception as the primary bottleneck. All tasks, images, provenance metadata, and evaluation code are released publicly.

title: Bridging Severe Cross-Modal Misalignment: End-to-End Visible-Infrared Object Detection via Explicit Feature-Domain Affine Registration
summary: Visible-infrared object detection relies on complementary RGB and thermal cues, but its performance is often degraded by cross-modal spatial misalignment. Most existing methods rely on implicit feature adaptation to handle weakly misaligned scenarios, while large-offset geometric discrepancies remain insufficiently addressed. In this paper, we propose a Joint Feature-domain Registration and Detection network (JFRDet), an end-to-end visible-infrared oriented object detector tailored for severely cross-modal geometric discrepancies. JFRDet introduces a Cross-Modal Affine Alignment (CMAA) module to estimate an image-level affine transformation for explicit multi-level feature alignment. Note that illumination changes directly affect the reliability of RGB cues, an Illumination-Guided Complementary Fusion (IGCF) module adaptively exploits modality reliability under varying illumination conditions for cross-modal fusion. Then, an Alignment Quality-Consistency Gating (AQCG) strategy stabilizes joint optimization by modulating detection supervision according to alignment reliability and gradient consistency. We further construct DroneVehicle Misaligned (DVMA), a benchmark for evaluating visible-infrared oriented object detection under severe cross-modal geometric misalignment. The proposed JFRDet achieves 69.7\% $\mathrm{mAP}_{50}$ on DVMA, which represents state-of-the-art (SOTA) performance. The code and dataset will be available on GitHub.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes JFRDet, an end-to-end visible-infrared oriented object detector that addresses severe cross-modal geometric misalignment through explicit feature-domain affine alignment, illumination-guided complementary fusion, and alignment quality-aware gating, achieving SOTA performance (69.7% mAP50) on a new DVMA benchmark.
AI.motivation: Existing visible-infrared object detection methods rely on implicit feature adaptation for weakly misaligned scenarios, but fail to handle large-offset geometric discrepancies between RGB and thermal images. This paper aims to address severe cross-modal geometric misalignment, which remains insufficiently addressed.
AI.method: JFRDet introduces three key components: (1) Cross-Modal Affine Alignment (CMAA) module for explicit image-level affine transformation and multi-level feature alignment; (2) Illumination-Guided Complementary Fusion (IGCF) module that adaptively exploits modality reliability under varying illumination; (3) Alignment Quality-Consistency Gating (AQCG) strategy that stabilizes joint optimization by modulating detection supervision based on alignment reliability and gradient consistency. A new benchmark, DVMA, was also constructed.
AI.result: JFRDet achieves 69.7% mAP50 on the DVMA benchmark, representing state-of-the-art performance on visible-infrared oriented object detection under severe cross-modal geometric misalignment.
AI.conclusion: Explicit geometric alignment combined with illumination-aware fusion and alignment-gated optimization effectively handles severe cross-modal misalignment in visible-infrared oriented object detection, and the authors plan to release code and dataset publicly.

title: Visual Geometry Foundation-Aware Gaussians for Single-Frame Surround-View Driving Reconstruction
summary: Single-frame surround-view reconstruction faces severe geometric instability and rendering artifacts due to minimal inter-camera overlap. While existing methods rely on complex decoders or auxiliary cues, they remain bottlenecked by the weak geometric capacity of upstream features. We argue that leveraging pretrained visual geometry priors strengthens upstream representations and alleviates the geometric ambiguity in sparse surround views. To this end, we propose VGGD, a visual geometry foundation-aware 3D Gaussian Splatting framework for feed-forward surround-view driving reconstruction, which shifts geometric modeling to the frontend and adapts foundation priors to the driving camera setting. First, VGGD leverages VGGT to provide transferable multi-view geometric prior tokens. Next, we introduce a Dual-Path Neck to decouple geometry-consistent and appearance-aware representations, improving appearance completion in weakly observed regions. We further apply Scale Warmup to stabilize early geometry learning and suppress scale drift under ego-pose changes. Finally, we use a hybrid pixel--volume Gaussian decoder to produce a renderable 3D Gaussian scene for novel-view synthesis. Experiments on the nuScenes single-frame benchmark show that VGGD achieves the best overall rendering quality among the compared methods and improves relative geometric consistency.

AI.tldr: VGGD is a visual geometry foundation-aware 3D Gaussian Splatting framework for feed-forward surround-view driving reconstruction. It uses VGGT to provide multi-view geometric priors, a Dual-Path Neck to decouple geometry/appearance representations, Scale Warmup for stable geometry learning, and a hybrid pixel-volume Gaussian decoder, achieving state-of-the-art rendering quality and geometric consistency on nuScenes.
AI.motivation: Single-frame surround-view reconstruction suffers from severe geometric instability and rendering artifacts due to minimal inter-camera overlap. Existing methods rely on complex decoders or auxiliary cues but are bottlenecked by weak geometric capacity of upstream features. The authors argue that pretrained visual geometry priors can strengthen upstream representations and alleviate geometric ambiguity in sparse surround views.
AI.method: VGGD shifts geometric modeling to the frontend using VGGT for transferable multi-view geometric prior tokens. It introduces a Dual-Path Neck to decouple geometry-consistent and appearance-aware representations for improved appearance completion in weakly observed regions, applies Scale Warmup to stabilize early geometry learning and suppress scale drift, and uses a hybrid pixel-volume Gaussian decoder for renderable 3D Gaussian scene generation.
AI.result: On the nuScenes single-frame benchmark, VGGD achieves the best overall rendering quality among compared methods and improves relative geometric consistency.
AI.conclusion: Leveraging pretrained visual geometry priors at the frontend of the pipeline effectively strengthens geometric representations and mitigates the geometric ambiguity inherent in sparse surround-view reconstruction, leading to superior rendering quality and geometric consistency.

title: Embedding Rotation Invariance for Provable Multi-Oriented Scene Text Recognition
summary: Multi-oriented text is ubiquitous in real-world scenes and remains a major challenge for scene text recognition (STR). Existing rotation-aware methods explicitly estimate text orientation. However, due to the lack of theoretical guarantees, they are prone to error accumulation, increased computational cost, and strong reliance on data. In this work, we incorporate rotation invariance into the STR framework to address these limitations. Specifically, we adopt an encoder-decoder architecture, embedding rotation equivariance in the encoder and rotation invariance in the decoder to construct a fully rotation-invariant network. On the decoder side, we first identify and prove the rotation-invariant property of the cross-attention mechanism and use it to formulate a rotation-invariant text decoder that maps visual features to output text in a rotation-invariant manner. On the encoder side, we propose a rotation-equivariant local-global extraction network that integrates deep equivariant convolutions with self-attention, enabling rotation-equivariant feature extraction while modeling inter-character dependencies and preserving fine-grained visual details. By integrating the encoder and decoder, we obtain an end-to-end Rotation-Invariant Scene Text Recognition network (RISTER). RISTER provides rotation invariance with theoretical guarantees, enhancing robustness on multi-oriented samples without introducing additional inference computation or relying on data-driven orientation correction. Experiments show that RISTER achieves state-of-the-art performance on both standard and multi-oriented benchmarks, surpassing the second-best model by 4.0 percent in accuracy on the general multi-oriented dataset.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces RISTER, a rotation-invariant scene text recognition network built on an encoder-decoder architecture with theoretically guaranteed rotation invariance—using rotation-equivariant convolutions in the encoder and a provably rotation-invariant cross-attention decoder—achieving state-of-the-art performance on multi-oriented text benchmarks without extra inference cost.
AI.motivation: Multi-oriented text in real-world scenes remains a major challenge for STR. Existing rotation-aware methods explicitly estimate orientation but suffer from error accumulation, increased computation, and heavy data dependence due to a lack of theoretical guarantees.
AI.method: The authors build a fully rotation-invariant network by embedding rotation equivariance in the encoder and rotation invariance in the decoder. The decoder uses cross-attention, which they prove is rotation-invariant, to map visual features to text. The encoder uses a rotation-equivariant local-global extraction network combining deep equivariant convolutions with self-attention to extract rotation-equivariant features while modeling inter-character dependencies and preserving fine details.
AI.result: RISTER achieves state-of-the-art performance on both standard and multi-oriented benchmarks, surpassing the second-best model by 4.0% accuracy on the general multi-oriented dataset, while requiring no additional inference computation or data-driven orientation correction.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating rotation invariance with theoretical guarantees into STR effectively addresses limitations of prior rotation-aware methods, improving robustness on multi-oriented samples without extra computational overhead.

title: MMArt A Multi-Perspective Multimodal Dataset for Visual Art Understanding
summary: Recent vision-language models demonstrate impressive general visual understanding, yet their art interpretation remains shallow: they describe surface content but struggle with formal analysis, grounded historical interpretation, or affective characterization. We argue this is not only a model but also a dataset limitation. Existing art datasets are single perspective resources, where no dataset provides narrative, formal, emotional, and historical perspectives simultaneously for the same artworks. We introduce MMArt, a large-scale dataset of 74,234 WikiArt paintings, each annotated with four independently annotated perspectives plus a harmonized unified caption, produced by specialized vision-language models or human annotation and validated through complementary quality evaluations. Two complementarity analyses establish that perspectives encode genuinely distinct information. A generative analysis shows that formal analysis descriptions best preserve compositional style, and historical descriptions carry strong affective signal in reconstructed images. A discriminative retrieval analysis reveals task-asymmetry: narrative descriptions drive retrieval (R@1 = 44.0%), while formal descriptions, strongest for reconstruction, are nearly nondiscriminative at retrieval scale (R@1 = 7.8%). Leave-one-out analysis further confirms that historical descriptions are the least replaceable perspective across both tasks. Together, the two analyses establish that no single perspective suffices for all tasks, directly motivating MMArt multi-perspective design. The dataset, code, and additional information are available at https://shuaiwang97.github.io/MMArt/.

AI.tldr: MMArt is a large-scale dataset of 74,234 WikiArt paintings, each annotated with four independent perspectives (narrative, formal, emotional, historical) plus a harmonized unified caption. The paper demonstrates through complementarity analyses that no single perspective suffices for all tasks, motivating the multi-perspective design.
AI.motivation: Vision-language models have shallow art interpretation—they describe surface content but fail at formal analysis, historical interpretation, and affective characterization. This stems from both model limitations and dataset limitations, as existing art datasets are single-perspective resources and none provide multiple perspectives simultaneously for the same artworks.
AI.method: The authors construct MMArt with 74,234 WikiArt paintings annotated across four independent perspectives plus a harmonized unified caption. Annotations are produced by specialized vision-language models or human annotation, validated through complementary quality evaluations. They conduct two complementarity analyses: a generative analysis (reconstruction quality preserving compositional style and affective signal) and a discriminative retrieval analysis (measuring retrieval performance across perspectives), plus a leave-one-out analysis.
AI.result: Formal analysis descriptions best preserve compositional style and historical descriptions carry strong affective signal in reconstructed images. Narrative descriptions drive retrieval (R@1 = 44.0%), while formal descriptions are nearly nondiscriminative at retrieval scale (R@1 = 7.8%). Leave-one-out analysis confirms historical descriptions are the least replaceable perspective across both tasks.
AI.conclusion: No single perspective suffices for all tasks, directly justifying the MMArt multi-perspective dataset design. The dataset, code, and additional information are publicly available.

title: Self-Geometry: GT-Free and Plug-and-Play Test-Time Adaptation for Geometrically Consistent 3D Vision Foundation Models
summary: Recent Vision Foundation Models (VFMs) predict depth, camera pose, and pointmap in a single forward pass without per-scene optimization, achieving strong generalization. However, enforcing explicit multi-view geometric consistency, e.g., through bundle adjustment, is computationally costly and is thus not imposed during VFM pretraining, so such inconsistency can arise. To address this, implicit self-consistency derived from model outputs (e.g., pointmaps, features), though enforced at test-time in prior work, delivers inherently limited performance gain, especially on scenes where the pretrained VFM is highly inaccurate. In contrast to this implicit signal, we propose Self-Geometry, a plug-and-play test-time adaptation pipeline that directly imposes explicit multi-view geometric constraints using 2D pixel correspondences as pseudo ground-truth. Our proposed Self-Geometry consists of Geometric Disentanglement Optimization, which combines Multi-View Consistency and Epipolar Consistency losses with Gradient Disentanglement to prevent gradient conflict; Frame Angular-Neighbor, a view sampler based on SO(3) geodesic distances for lightly imposing these constraints; and Lightweight TTA, which adapts VFMs via LoRA. Our method achieves consistent improvements in both pose and geometry estimation across six VFMs (VGGT, $π^3$, DA3-Giant/Large/Base/Small) and four benchmarks (7Scenes, ETH3D, ScanNet++, HiRoom).

AI.tldr: Self-Geometry is a plug-and-play test-time adaptation pipeline that enforces explicit multi-view geometric constraints using 2D pixel correspondences as pseudo ground-truth to improve Vision Foundation Models' camera pose and geometry estimation.
AI.motivation: Vision Foundation Models predict depth, pose, and pointmaps in a single forward pass without per-scene optimization, but they lack explicit multi-view geometric consistency because bundle adjustment is too costly during pretraining. Prior test-time methods using implicit self-consistency signals deliver limited gains, especially on scenes where the pretrained VFM is highly inaccurate.
AI.method: Self-Geometry includes three components: (1) Geometric Disentanglement Optimization, which combines Multi-View Consistency and Epipolar Consistency losses with Gradient Disentanglement to prevent gradient conflicts; (2) Frame Angular-Neighbor, a view sampler based on SO(3) geodesic distances for lightly imposing constraints; and (3) Lightweight TTA, which adapts VFMs via LoRA at test time.
AI.result: The method achieves consistent improvements in both pose and geometry estimation across six VFMs (VGGT, π³, DA3-Giant/Large/Base/Small) and four benchmarks (7Scenes, ETH3D, ScanNet++, HiRoom).
AI.conclusion: Explicit multi-view geometric constraints using pseudo ground-truth from 2D pixel correspondences can effectively improve VFM test-time performance, outperforming implicit self-consistency approaches, and this plug-and-play adaptation is generalizable across various VFMs and benchmarks.

title: Compact Feed-Forward 3D Gaussians via Saliency-Guided Primitive Merging
summary: 3D scene reconstruction, modeling, and rendering are highly relevant for numerous tasks, and 3D Gaussian splatting has become a standard choice in this context. Its feed-forward variants provide fast reconstruction from sparse input views but often produce per-pixel primitives, leading to highly redundant and thus inefficient representations. We present a structure-aware merging pipeline that takes per-pixel primitives from any feed-forward method and consolidates them into a compact, content-adaptive Gaussian set while largely retaining visual quality at just $\frac{1}{20}^\text{th}$ of the Gaussians of a per-pixel method. We group spatially coherent Gaussians of similar appearance into variable-size clusters via adaptive superpixel segmentation guided by a saliency map, which allocates fine segments to textured regions and coarse segments to homogeneous areas. We compress each cluster into a compact latent representation through a learned encoder, then match and consolidate representations across views based on geometric overlap and feature similarity via a learned merger. A level-of-detail decoder then produces the final Gaussians at a controllable resolution, enabling a flexible quality-efficiency trade-off at inference. As a post-processing module, the pipeline is backbone-agnostic, leveraging the strengths of existing feed-forward methods. This leads to better and more robust quality than achieved by previous approaches that target a reduction in primitive count, while providing a highly compact representation, that can be rendered efficiently.

AI.tldr: This paper presents a structure-aware merging pipeline that consolidates per-pixel Gaussian primitives from any feed-forward 3D reconstruction method into a compact, content-adaptive Gaussian set, reducing the primitive count to 1/20th while largely preserving visual quality.
AI.motivation: Feed-forward 3D Gaussian splatting variants produce per-pixel primitives that are highly redundant and inefficient, lacking compactness for practical use.
AI.method: The pipeline groups spatially coherent Gaussians of similar appearance into variable-size clusters via adaptive superpixel segmentation guided by a saliency map, compresses each cluster into a compact latent representation with a learned encoder, matches and consolidates representations across views based on geometric overlap and feature similarity via a learned merger, and uses a level-of-detail decoder to produce final Gaussians at controllable resolution.
AI.result: The method achieves better and more robust quality than previous approaches targeting primitive count reduction, while providing a highly compact representation at 1/20th of the Gaussians of a per-pixel method, renderable efficiently.
AI.conclusion: As a backbone-agnostic post-processing module, the pipeline leverages the strengths of existing feed-forward methods, enabling a flexible quality-efficiency trade-off at inference and offering an efficient, compact 3D representation.

title: Grid-Preserving Knowledge Distillation: Transferring Convolutional Inductive Bias to Vision Transformers under Data Scarcity
summary: Vision Transformers underperform convolutional networks when training data is scarce, and distilling convolutional inductive biases from a CNN teacher is an effective remedy that leaves the deployed model unchanged. General-purpose feature distillation, however, transfers little in this setting. The pooling, flattening, and logit-space projections it inherits from CNN to CNN pipelines discard the spatial grid in which locality and translation equivariance are encoded, and unlike a convolutional student, a ViT cannot rebuild that structure on its own. In this paper, we propose iBKD, a distillation framework that preserves the grid along the entire transfer path. Its core module, the Inductive Bias Attention Module, aggregates every student layer onto the teacher grid with learned weights, sharpens structural cues with channel and deformable spatial attention, and injects them through convolutional cross-attention that operates between grids rather than between token sets. The module is used only during training, so the deployed model is an unmodified ViT with no inference overhead. Across seven Transformer backbones and six data-scarce benchmarks, iBKD outperforms both locality-guidance methods and general knowledge distillation baselines, and its margin widens as training data shrinks.

AI.tldr: iBKD is a distillation framework that preserves the spatial grid when transferring inductive biases from CNN teachers to Vision Transformer students, using an Inductive Bias Attention Module that aggregates student layers, sharpens structural cues, and injects them via convolutional cross-attention—all without adding inference overhead to the deployed model.
AI.motivation: Vision Transformers underperform CNNs under data scarcity because they lack inductive biases like locality and translation equivariance. Distilling these biases from a CNN teacher is effective, but existing feature distillation methods discard the spatial grid structure during transfer, and ViTs cannot rebuild this structure on their own unlike convolutional students.
AI.method: The paper proposes iBKD, a distillation framework with a core Inductive Bias Attention Module that: (1) aggregates every student layer onto the teacher's spatial grid with learned weights, (2) sharpens structural cues using channel and deformable spatial attention, and (3) injects them through convolutional cross-attention operating between grids rather than token sets. The module is used only during training, keeping the deployed ViT unmodified with no inference overhead.
AI.result: Across seven Transformer backbones and six data-scarce benchmarks, iBKD outperforms both locality-guidance methods and general knowledge distillation baselines. The performance margin widens as training data shrinks.
AI.conclusion: iBKD effectively transfers CNN inductive biases to ViTs under data scarcity by preserving the spatial grid throughout distillation, achieving superior performance with no inference cost on the deployed model.

title: InterPruner: Interactive Structured Pruning via Taylor-Implicit Criterion and Language-Prior Modulator for Multimodal Object Detection
summary: Multimodal object detection proves effective in remote sensing, especially the RGB-Infrared paradigm. The parallel feature extractors provide rich multimodal information for robust detection, yet introduce substantial channel redundancy and computational overhead. Existing pruning methods can reduce channel redundancy, but they are designed for unimodal backbones, overlooking cross-modal interactions and dynamic scene-wise redundancy. In this paper, we propose InterPruner, the first interactive structured channel pruning framework for RGB-infrared object detectors. Specifically, we first derive a Taylor-Implicit Criterion(TIC) to quantify channel importance via high-order Taylor expansion and the implicit function theorem. Then, a Modality Interaction Redundancy Analyzer (MIRA) identifies redundant channels via mutual compensability assessment. Finally, a Scene-Prior Channel Anchor (SPCA) uses language priors as semantic anchors to measure channel-scene relevance for dynamic channel importance estimation. Cross-modality channel pruning for RGB-Infrared detection is yet unexplored. Extensive experiments on RGB-infrared object detection dataset demonstrate that InterPruner maintains high performance with negligible degradation. Specifically, it even achieves a 0.6% mAP increase on the FLIR dataset when pruning 50% of the channels. Code will be available on GitHub to facilitate future work.

AI.tldr: InterPruner is the first interactive structured channel pruning framework for RGB-infrared object detectors, using a Taylor-Implicit Criterion for channel importance, a Modality Interaction Redundancy Analyzer for cross-modal redundancy, and a Scene-Prior Channel Anchor for dynamic scene-aware pruning, achieving up to 0.6% mAP increase at 50% channel pruning on FLIR.
AI.motivation: Existing pruning methods are designed for unimodal backbones and overlook cross-modal interactions and dynamic scene-wise redundancy in RGB-infrared object detection, where parallel feature extractors introduce substantial channel redundancy and computational overhead.
AI.method: InterPruner comprises three components: (1) Taylor-Implicit Criterion (TIC) quantifies channel importance via high-order Taylor expansion and the implicit function theorem; (2) Modality Interaction Redundancy Analyzer (MIRA) identifies redundant channels via mutual compensability assessment; (3) Scene-Prior Channel Anchor (SPCA) uses language priors as semantic anchors to measure channel-scene relevance for dynamic channel importance estimation.
AI.result: Experiments on RGB-infrared object detection datasets show InterPruner maintains high performance with negligible degradation, and even achieves a 0.6% mAP increase on the FLIR dataset when pruning 50% of channels.
AI.conclusion: Cross-modality channel pruning for RGB-infrared detection is a novel and unexplored direction, and InterPruner demonstrates its effectiveness, with code to be released on GitHub to facilitate future work.

title: Rethinking LLM Verification: Evidence Structure, Uncertainty, and Selective Refinement
comment: Findings Track at the Conference on Empirical Methods in Natural Language Processing (EMNLP 2026)
summary: Large language models (LLMs) often rely on shortcuts rather than systematic reasoning, raising safety concerns in medical applications. Allowing models to abstain when uncertain improves reliability but introduces a coverage accuracy tradeoff. We propose a two-stage framework for medical hypothesis verification in multiple-choice settings that manages this tradeoff through targeted ontology grounding, applied only when the model abstains. We show that abstention is not random but reflects genuine uncertainty, with abstained predictions associated with lower confidence. Across two frontier models (GPT-5.5, accessed via the Azure OpenAI API, and DeepSeek-R1), the proposed framework improves question-level accuracy by 9.6 percentage points (82.9% to 92.5%) and hypothesis-level accuracy by 4.2 percentage points (92.0% to 96.2%). Our experiments conducted on MedReason and MedQA show that abstention can be repurposed as a control signal for selective reasoning refinement, achieving knowledge-graph-level performance without explicit knowledge graph construction.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a two-stage framework for medical hypothesis verification in multiple-choice settings that leverages abstention as a control signal to apply targeted ontology grounding only when the model is uncertain. This approach improves question-level accuracy by 9.6 percentage points and hypothesis-level accuracy by 4.2 percentage points across GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-R1 on MedReason and MedQA benchmarks.
AI.motivation: LLMs often rely on shortcuts rather than systematic reasoning, which is problematic for medical applications. While allowing models to abstain when uncertain improves reliability, it introduces a coverage-accuracy tradeoff. The authors aim to manage this tradeoff by repurposing abstention as a signal for targeted reasoning refinement.
AI.method: The framework is two-stage: (1) the model first attempts medical hypothesis verification with an option to abstain; (2) when the model abstains, targeted ontology grounding is applied selectively to refine reasoning. This selective application avoids the cost of full ontology grounding while addressing genuine uncertainty.
AI.result: Across two frontier models (GPT-5.5 and DeepSeek-R1), the framework improves question-level accuracy by 9.6 percentage points (82.9% to 92.5%) and hypothesis-level accuracy by 4.2 percentage points (92.0% to 96.2%) on MedReason and MedQA benchmarks.
AI.conclusion: Abstention is not random but reflects genuine uncertainty, and can be repurposed as a control signal for selective reasoning refinement. The framework achieves knowledge-graph-level performance without explicit knowledge graph construction.

title: Beyond Pixels: From Video Priors to 4D Worlds
summary: 4D generation synthesizes dynamic 3D scenes from conditions such as text or images. Existing methods either reconstruct generated RGB videos with a separate 4D model or adapt a particular video generator to predict geometry directly. The former suffers from distribution mismatch and error propagation, whereas the latter ties 4D prediction to a specific generator and may require retraining when the generator or conditioning regime changes. We ask whether the final denoised latents of video models that share a variational autoencoder (VAE) can instead provide a reusable interface to explicit 4D prediction. Building on this insight, we introduce direct latent-to-4D generation and instantiate it as Latent-to-4D, which bypasses RGB by aligning a video latent with the token grid of a pretrained 4D decoder and refining it through frame-wise and global spatiotemporal attention. Trained on roughly 1K existing reconstruction clips, a single checkpoint transfers unchanged across multiple video diffusion transformers within the same VAE family. On Text4D-200 and I4D-200, Latent-to-4D surpasses matched same-latent Wan+4RC cascades in projection-based DINO-F1 by 2.88--3.45 and 5.81 points, respectively, while also being preferred by human raters for geometry, temporal stability, and overall quality.

AI.tldr: Latent-to-4D proposes using the final denoised latents of video diffusion models (that share a VAE) as a reusable interface for direct 4D generation, bypassing RGB video intermediate steps. It aligns video latents with the token grid of a pretrained 4D decoder and refines them with spatiotemporal attention, achieving state-of-the-art results on Text4D-200 and I4D-200 benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Existing 4D generation methods either reconstruct RGB videos from separate 4D models (suffering from distribution mismatch and error propagation) or adapt specific video generators to predict geometry directly (tying 4D prediction to a particular generator and requiring retraining when the generator changes). The paper asks whether shared-VAE video latent spaces can serve as a reusable interface to explicit 4D prediction.
AI.method: Latent-to-4D directly performs latent-to-4D generation by aligning a video latent with the token grid of a pretrained 4D decoder and refining it through frame-wise and global spatiotemporal attention. It is trained on roughly 1K existing reconstruction clips, and a single checkpoint transfers across multiple video diffusion transformers within the same VAE family without retraining.
AI.result: On Text4D-200 and I4D-200, Latent-to-4D surpasses matched same-latent Wan+4RC cascades in projection-based DINO-F1 by 2.88-3.45 and 5.81 points respectively, and is preferred by human raters for geometry, temporal stability, and overall quality.
AI.conclusion: Latent-to-4D demonstrates that shared-VAE video latents provide a reusable interface for explicit 4D prediction, enabling a single model to work across multiple video generators without retraining while outperforming cascade approaches.

title: Where To Look? : Causal Tracing of Vision Encoders in VLM
summary: Vision-language models can describe an image with remarkable accuracy, yet a more fundamental question remains unanswered: what visual information actually drives their answers? In this work, we investigate this question through causal tracing, and we observe that highly causal vision tokens often lie outside the target region. Extending the analysis to larger vision-language models reveals a similar pattern across models and corruption settings, suggesting that strong multimodal performance does not necessarily imply spatially localized causal representations. We further investigate: can these models preserve visual structure when appearance cues are removed? and find that visual cues are exploited to understand visual structures. Together, our experiments expose a gap between seeing, using, and reasoning over visual structure, and provide a causal framework for studying how visual information is transformed, preserved, and ultimately used by modern vision-language models.

AI.tldr: This paper uses causal tracing to investigate what visual information actually drives vision-language model (VLM) answers, finding that highly causal vision tokens often lie outside the target region across multiple models and settings. The study reveals that strong multimodal performance does not imply spatially localized causal representations, and that models exploit appearance cues rather than genuinely reasoning over visual structure.
AI.motivation: While VLMs can describe images accurately, it remains unclear what visual information actually drives their responses. The authors aim to address this fundamental question about which visual tokens causally influence model outputs, and whether visual structure is truly being reasoned over or simply exploited through appearance cues.
AI.method: The study employs causal tracing to identify highly causal vision tokens in VLMs, extends the analysis across larger models and corruption settings, and conducts experiments that remove appearance cues to test whether models can still preserve and reason over visual structure.
AI.result: Highly causal vision tokens are often found outside the target region. This pattern is consistent across larger VLMs and various corruption settings, indicating that strong multimodal performance does not necessarily correspond to spatially localized causal representations. Visual appearance cues are exploited by models to understand visual structures rather than genuinely reasoning over them.
AI.conclusion: The experiments expose a gap between seeing, using, and reasoning over visual structure in modern VLMs. The paper provides a causal framework for studying how visual information is transformed, preserved, and ultimately used by vision-language models.

title: FADE: From Passive Verification to Active Discovery in Counterfactual Video Understanding
summary: Counterfactual video understanding evaluates whether models grasp physical and commonsense regularities. However, existing multiple-choice question (MCQ) benchmarks inadvertently leak target events through their questions and candidate options. This reduces the core challenge from active discovery to text-guided verification. In this paper, we present FADE, an effective training framework for counterfactual discovery and explanation. Our method is built on an evidence-first, two-stage training paradigm. First, evidence-internalized supervised fine-tuning grounds the model's predictions in decisive visual anomalies. Second, we apply a fading-anchor reinforcement learning strategy that progressively removes textual guidance, compelling the model to independently discover and explain evidence. To rigorously evaluate this capability, we also introduce an effective pipeline that converts existing MCQ datasets into aligned MCQ, open-ended question answering (OQA), and captioning tasks without requiring additional data curation. Our simple approach yields strong results. Using Qwen3-VL-8B as the baseline, FADE achieves state-of-the-art strict paired scores across all three tasks on DualityVidQA-test and IPV-Bench, outperforming GPT-5.6. In specific, when transitioning from constrained MCQs to unconstrained OQA and captioning, our model demonstrates remarkable robustness. Its performance retention is 90.4% and 67.4% on DualityVidQA-test-substantially higher than the 48.1% and 30.7% retained by GPT-5.6. We hope this simple framework can serve as a solid baseline for future research in unconstrained counterfactual video understanding.

AI.tldr: FADE is a two-stage training framework for counterfactual video understanding that combines evidence-internalized supervised fine-tuning with a fading-anchor reinforcement learning strategy. It converts MCQ benchmarks into aligned MCQ, OQA, and captioning tasks, achieving state-of-the-art results on DualityVidQA-test and IPV-Bench, with significantly higher performance retention (90.4%/67.4% vs GPT-5.6's 48.1%/30.7%) when transitioning from constrained to unconstrained tasks.
AI.motivation: Existing counterfactual video understanding MCQ benchmarks inadvertently leak target events through their questions and candidate options, reducing the task from active discovery to text-guided verification. This undermines the evaluation of whether models truly grasp physical and commonsense regularities.
AI.method: FADE employs a two-stage training paradigm: (1) evidence-internalized supervised fine-tuning that grounds model predictions in decisive visual anomalies, followed by (2) a fading-anchor reinforcement learning strategy that progressively removes textual guidance, compelling the model to independently discover and explain evidence. They also introduce a pipeline to convert existing MCQ datasets into aligned MCQ, open-ended question answering (OQA), and captioning tasks without additional data curation.
AI.result: Using Qwen3-VL-8B as the baseline, FADE achieves state-of-the-art strict paired scores across all three tasks on DualityVidQA-test and IPV-Bench, outperforming GPT-5.6. Performance retention from MCQs to OQA is 90.4% and to captioning is 67.4% on DualityVidQA-test, substantially higher than GPT-5.6's 48.1% and 30.7%.
AI.conclusion: FADE provides a simple yet effective framework for unconstrained counterfactual video understanding, serving as a solid baseline for future research in this area.

title: MVTrack: Ultrafast Appearance-Free Moving Object Tracking from Compressed Bitstreams
comment: This paper has been accepted to the 2nd workshop on Low-Level Vision Frontiers with Generative AI, Preference Optimization, Agentic Systems and World Models (LoViF) at ECCV2026
summary: Deploying modern video trackers at scale is bottlenecked by the computational cost of RGB-based object detectors. To this end, we present MVTrack, an ultrafast tracker for moving objects that operates directly on H.264 bitstreams. MVTrack combines MVDet, a lightweight detector for motion vector fields, with MVLink, a minimalist kinematic association module. On VIRAT, MVTrack outperforms YOLO26n while using 60$\times$ fewer parameters, requiring 40$\times$ fewer FLOPs, and reducing CPU latency by 8.6$\times$. These results demonstrate that compressed video data alone can enable accurate and scalable surveillance tracking, thereby bypassing the need for pixel reconstruction.

AI.tldr: MVTrack is an ultrafast moving-object tracker that operates directly on H.264 bitstreams, combining MVDet (a lightweight detector for motion vector fields) with MVLink (a minimalist kinematic association module). It outperforms YOLO26n on VIRAT while using 60x fewer parameters, 40x fewer FLOPs, and 8.6x lower CPU latency, demonstrating that compressed video data alone can enable accurate and scalable surveillance tracking without pixel reconstruction.
AI.motivation: Deploying modern video trackers at scale is bottlenecked by the computational cost of RGB-based object detectors, making efficient tracking in compressed video streams a pressing need.
AI.method: MVTrack operates directly on H.264 bitstreams using two components: MVDet, a lightweight detector that processes motion vector fields, and MVLink, a minimalist kinematic association module for tracking.
AI.result: On VIRAT, MVTrack outperforms YOLO26n while using 60x fewer parameters, requiring 40x fewer FLOPs, and reducing CPU latency by 8.6x.
AI.conclusion: Compressed video data alone can enable accurate and scalable surveillance tracking, bypassing the need for pixel reconstruction.

title: E$^3$mo-Bench: A Scalable Benchmark for Multimodal Evoked and Expressed Emotion Understanding via Bayesian Pairwise Alignment
summary: Understanding both expressed and evoked emotions is critical for multimodal large language models (MLLMs) to achieve comprehensive affect-aware interactions. However, existing benchmarks typically examine expressed and evoked emotions in isolation or are constrained to coarse-grained and incomplete affective characterizations. To bridge this gap, we introduce E$^3$mo-Bench, a scalable benchmark comprising $12{,}314$ question-answer pairs across $2{,}524$ videos with predefined affective perspectives. It evaluates evoked and expressed emotion understanding via $3$ complementary tasks: emotion perception, open-vocabulary recognition, and valence-arousal-dominance (VAD) assessment. To efficiently scale reliable continuous annotations, we propose Bayesian Pairwise Alignment, which aggregates sparse, low-burden pairwise judgments into anchor-referenced VAD estimates. Furthermore, we develop E$^3$mo-Score, a training-free agent that aggregates complementary judgments from a five-model committee to improve VAD estimation. Extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of our framework and expose a pronounced performance skew between evoked and expressed emotion paradigms. These findings, coupled with MLLMs' persistent deficits in fine-grained recognition and dimensional assessment, chart a clear course for advancing multimodal emotional intelligence.

AI.tldr: E3mo-Bench is a scalable benchmark with 12,314 QA pairs across 2,524 videos for evaluating MLLMs on both evoked and expressed emotion understanding through three complementary tasks: emotion perception, open-vocabulary recognition, and VAD assessment. It introduces Bayesian Pairwise Alignment for efficient continuous annotation scaling and E3mo-Score, a training-free agent aggregating judgments from a five-model committee.
AI.motivation: Existing benchmarks examine expressed and evoked emotions in isolation or use coarse-grained, incomplete affective characterizations. There is a need to bridge this gap by providing a comprehensive benchmark that evaluates both emotion paradigms simultaneously with fine-grained affective understanding.
AI.method: The paper introduces E3mo-Bench, a benchmark with three complementary tasks (emotion perception, open-vocabulary recognition, and valence-arousal-dominance assessment). It proposes Bayesian Pairwise Alignment for aggregating sparse pairwise judgments into anchor-referenced VAD estimates to scale reliable annotations, and E3mo-Score, a training-free agent that combines judgments from a five-model committee.
AI.result: Extensive experiments validate the framework's effectiveness and reveal a pronounced performance skew between evoked and expressed emotion paradigms. MLLMs show persistent deficits in fine-grained recognition and dimensional assessment.
AI.conclusion: The findings chart a clear course for advancing multimodal emotional intelligence by highlighting the need to address the performance gap between evoked and expressed emotion understanding, as well as improving fine-grained recognition and dimensional emotion assessment in MLLMs.

title: Beyond Fixed Luminance: Towards Panchromatic and Orthochromatic Image Colorization
summary: Most image colorization systems operate in $Lab$ space by predicting chroma ($ab$) while preserving an input-derived luminance channel ($L$). While effective on standard benchmarks, this fixed-luminance design restricts brightness changes and becomes unreliable when grayscale formation deviates from natural-image luminance, as in historical orthochromatic photography. We propose a luminance-agnostic colorization framework that formulates colorization as full-RGB image editing using a foundation image-editing model. To bridge modern panchromatic and historical orthochromatic conditions, we introduce a mixed grayscale objective that trains the model under both standard luminance grayscale and a red-insensitive grayscale formation. Experiments on COCO, ImageNet, and a multi-instance benchmark show that our method is competitive on standard grayscale inputs and substantially more robust under orthochromatic inputs, with qualitative comparisons and a human study indicating fewer visible color artifacts.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a luminance-agnostic colorization framework that reformulates colorization as full-RGB image editing using a foundation image-editing model, trained with a mixed grayscale objective to handle both standard panchromatic and historical orthochromatic (red-insensitive) grayscale inputs.
AI.motivation: Traditional colorization systems operate in Lab space by predicting chroma while keeping the input luminance fixed. This design restricts brightness changes and fails when grayscale formation deviates from natural-image luminance, such as in historical orthochromatic photography.
AI.method: Formulates colorization as full-RGB image editing using a foundation image-editing model, and introduces a mixed grayscale objective that trains the model under both standard luminance grayscale and red-insensitive (orthochromatic) grayscale formation.
AI.result: On COCO, ImageNet, and a multi-instance benchmark, the method is competitive on standard grayscale inputs and substantially more robust under orthochromatic inputs. Qualitative comparisons and a human study show fewer visible color artifacts.
AI.conclusion: A luminance-agnostic, foundation-model-based colorization approach that generalizes across both modern and historical grayscale formation conditions, improving robustness for orthochromatic inputs without sacrificing performance on standard inputs.

title: Evaluating Semantic and Spatial Guidance for Foundation Model Segmentation of Small-Scale PV in Remote Sensing Imagery
summary: Spatio-temporal PV data are essential for understanding adoption processes in off-grid regions, yet such data remain largely unavailable. Automated segmentation of remote sensing (RS) imagery offers a promising solution; yet, residential PV systems remain challenging targets because of their small size and sparse distribution, resulting in severe target-background imbalance. Vision-language foundation models (FMs) provide a data-efficient paradigm through prompt-based semantic and spatial guidance, but the relative contribution of different prompt types remains unclear. We systematically evaluate SAM3 for small-scale PV segmentation in RS imagery by comparing textual, geometric, and hybrid prompting, under varying supervision levels, training strategies, spatial resolutions, and imaging conditions. Multi-temporal aerial imagery from a large off-grid rural region serves as a study site, with findings validated across three additional datasets. Prompting strategy emerged as the dominant factor governing model behavior. Textual prompting consistently produced the lowest performance and showed the greatest sensitivity to supervision and imaging conditions. In contrast, spatial guidance substantially improved both segmentation accuracy and robustness. Hybrid prompting achieved the highest accuracy and stability, indicating that semantic and spatial guidance provide complementary information. Most performance gains were achieved with only a few hundred annotated samples, demonstrating strong data efficiency. Transfer learning had limited overall impact, with only modest improvements observed for textual prompting under limited supervision. Overall, our findings establish prompting strategy as a key determinant of SAM3 adaptation, robustness, and generalization, highlighting the potential of promptable FMs for scalable PV mapping in data-constrained off-grid regions.

AI.tldr: This paper systematically evaluates SAM3 (a vision-language foundation model) for small-scale residential PV segmentation in remote sensing imagery from off-grid rural regions, comparing textual, geometric, and hybrid prompting strategies under various conditions. Hybrid prompting (combining semantic and spatial guidance) achieved the best accuracy and robustness, while prompting strategy was identified as the dominant factor governing model behavior and data efficiency.
AI.motivation: Spatio-temporal PV data are critical for understanding adoption processes in off-grid regions but remain largely unavailable due to the difficulty of detecting small, sparsely distributed residential PV systems in remote sensing imagery. While vision-language foundation models offer a data-efficient paradigm through prompt-based guidance, the relative contributions of different prompt types (textual vs. spatial vs. hybrid) have not been systematically investigated.
AI.method: The authors systematically evaluate SAM3 for small-scale PV segmentation in remote sensing imagery, comparing textual, geometric, and hybrid prompting strategies while varying supervision levels, training strategies, spatial resolutions, and imaging conditions. Multi-temporal aerial imagery from a large off-grid rural region serves as the primary study site, with findings validated across three additional datasets.
AI.result: Prompting strategy emerged as the dominant factor governing model behavior. Textual prompting produced the lowest performance with the greatest sensitivity to supervision and imaging conditions. Spatial guidance substantially improved both segmentation accuracy and robustness. Hybrid prompting achieved the highest accuracy and stability. Most performance gains were achieved with only a few hundred annotated samples, demonstrating strong data efficiency. Transfer learning had limited overall impact, with only modest improvements for textual prompting under limited supervision.
AI.conclusion: The findings establish prompting strategy as a key determinant of SAM3 adaptation, robustness, and generalization, highlighting the potential of promptable foundation models for scalable PV mapping in data-constrained off-grid regions.

title: BPG: Balancing Plasticity and Generalization for Domain Incremental Learning
summary: Deep neural networks excel in various tasks but struggle to generalize across evolving data distributions, leading to significant performance degradation under domain shifts. Domain incremental learning (DIL) addresses this challenge by enabling models to continuously adapt while retaining prior knowledge. Among existing DIL approaches, the parameter-isolation paradigm achieves state-of-the-art performance. However, these methods often adopt a one-size-fits-all approach to adapt to new domains, resulting in either insufficient learning capacity or redundant parameters. In this work, we propose BPG, a unified framework that addresses both challenges through two complementary components: BPG-Adapter, which dynamically determines each domain's adapter hidden dimension based on domain-specific feature separability, and BPG-Inference, a soft domain mixture strategy that integrates multiple domain-specific models at test time, mitigating domain ID misselection. Experimental results on DomainNet, CDDB, and CORe50 demonstrate that BPG consistently outperforms uniform adapter-based approaches and hard domain selection strategies, achieving state-of-the-art average accuracy while reducing forgetting to as low as 0.22% on DomainNet.

AI.tldr: BPG is a unified framework for domain incremental learning that dynamically determines adapter hidden dimensions per domain based on feature separability and employs a soft domain mixture strategy at inference time, achieving state-of-the-art accuracy while reducing forgetting to as low as 0.22% on DomainNet.
AI.motivation: Existing parameter-isolation-based domain incremental learning methods adopt a one-size-fits-all approach to adapt to new domains, which leads to either insufficient learning capacity or redundant parameters.
AI.method: BPG consists of two components: BPG-Adapter, which dynamically determines each domain's adapter hidden dimension based on domain-specific feature separability, and BPG-Inference, a soft domain mixture strategy that integrates multiple domain-specific models at test time to mitigate domain ID misselection.
AI.result: Experiments on DomainNet, CDDB, and CORe50 show BPG consistently outperforms uniform adapter-based approaches and hard domain selection strategies, achieving state-of-the-art average accuracy and reducing forgetting to as low as 0.22% on DomainNet.
AI.conclusion: BPG effectively addresses both insufficient learning capacity and redundant parameter allocation in DIL through adaptive adapter sizing and soft domain mixture inference, setting a new state-of-the-art benchmark.

title: Fast and Memory-Efficient Wavelet Convolutions via I/O-Aware Reformulation
summary: Wavelet convolution (WTConv) has emerged as an increasingly popular drop-in replacement for standard convolutions, expanding a network's receptive field exponentially with the number of decomposition levels while keeping the parameter count linear. However, its reference implementation is severely memory-bound due to excessive data movement through high-bandwidth memory (HBM). We develop an I/O model of WTConv to characterize this bottleneck and use it to guide three algebraic reformulations: (1) recomputing the inexpensive Haar analysis butterfly on chip, (2) collapsing the multi-level synthesis cascade into a single closed-form pass indexed by output-coordinate bits, and (3) folding learned per-channel scales into the convolution weights. Together, these reformulations enable an I/O-aware fused implementation that substantially reduces HBM traffic. We evaluate the WTConvNeXt configuration across decomposition levels and a broad range of tensor shapes. Despite performing comparable arithmetic, the reference WTConv is substantially slower than the depthwise convolution it replaces. Our reformulation reduces modeled HBM traffic by approximately $2.55\times$, yielding up to a $4.35\times$ training speedup over the reference while roughly halving peak memory usage. Thus, our reformulation preserves the benefits of WTConv while substantially reducing its execution time and memory footprint, removing the systems overhead that previously limited its practical efficiency.

AI.tldr: This paper addresses the memory-bound inefficiency of Wavelet Convolution (WTConv), a drop-in replacement for standard convolutions that expands receptive fields exponentially. The authors develop an I/O model to characterize HBM traffic bottlenecks and introduce three algebraic reformulations: on-chip recomputation of the Haar butterfly, collapsing the multi-level synthesis cascade into a single closed-form pass, and folding per-channel scales into convolution weights. These yield an I/O-aware fused implementation that reduces modeled HBM traffic by ~2.55x, achieves up to 4.35x training speedup over the reference, and roughly halves peak memory usage while preserving WTConv's benefits.
AI.motivation: WTConv is an attractive drop-in replacement for standard convolutions due to its exponential receptive field growth with linear parameter count, but its reference implementation is severely memory-bound due to excessive data movement through high-bandwidth memory (HBM), limiting its practical efficiency.
AI.method: The authors develop an I/O model of WTConv to characterize the HBM bottleneck, then use it to guide three algebraic reformulations: (1) recomputing the inexpensive Haar analysis butterfly on chip, (2) collapsing the multi-level synthesis cascade into a single closed-form pass indexed by output-coordinate bits, and (3) folding learned per-channel scales into the convolution weights. These enable an I/O-aware fused implementation that substantially reduces HBM traffic.
AI.result: The reformulation reduces modeled HBM traffic by approximately 2.55x, yielding up to a 4.35x training speedup over the reference implementation while roughly halving peak memory usage, evaluated on WTConvNeXt across decomposition levels and a broad range of tensor shapes.
AI.conclusion: The reformulation preserves the benefits of WTConv while substantially reducing execution time and memory footprint, removing the systems overhead that previously limited its practical efficiency and enabling broader adoption of WTConv as a practical alternative to standard convolutions.

title: Modelling Geographic Atrophy Progression using Implicit Neural Representations
summary: Age-related Macular Degeneration (AMD) is the major cause of blindness in the Western world. Its late dry phase is characterised by irreversible atrophic areas, namely Geographic Atrophy (GA). Longitudinal Fundus Autofluorescence (FAF) image acquisitions are currently the main tool for assessing lesion growth over time at the image level. However, due to its highly individualised progression, the evolution of late AMD remains poorly understood. In this work, we propose using Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) to model GA progression at the individual level in a low-data setting. Our approach generates both FAF and GA segmentation at both past and future time points. Among the comparison models, our method achieves competitive segmentation quality across different scenarios, yielding the lowest Mean Absolute Error (MAE) for the GA lesion area and the highest DICE score, without sacrificing FAF image quality. The code is available at https://github.com/SimoneSarrocco/ga-progression-with-inrs.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes using Implicit Neural Representations (INRs) to model Geographic Atrophy progression in Age-related Macular Degeneration from longitudinal Fundus Autofluorescence images, generating both FAF images and GA segmentations at past and future time points in a low-data setting. The method achieves the lowest MAE for GA lesion area and highest DICE score among comparison models without sacrificing FAF image quality.
AI.motivation: Late dry AMD progression is highly individualized and poorly understood. Current approaches assess lesion growth at the image level using longitudinal FAF acquisitions, but modeling the evolution of GA at the individual level remains challenging, especially in low-data settings.
AI.method: The approach uses Implicit Neural Representations to model GA progression at the individual patient level. The INR is trained on longitudinal FAF images and corresponding GA segmentations, and is capable of generating both FAF images and GA segmentation maps at arbitrary (past and future) time points.
AI.result: The method achieves competitive segmentation quality across different scenarios, attaining the lowest Mean Absolute Error (MAE) for the GA lesion area and the highest DICE score among compared models, while maintaining FAF image quality.
AI.conclusion: INRs provide an effective approach for modeling individual-level GA progression in low-data settings, generating both images and segmentations at arbitrary time points with strong performance.

title: MIRA: Medical Image Reflection for Agentic Diagnosis
summary: Medical visual agents can use tools to inspect images and retrieve external knowledge, but indiscriminate tool use may introduce noisy or misleading evidence. Reliable diagnosis therefore requires not only acquiring additional observations, but also verifying whether tool actions are necessary and whether the resulting evidence supports the current hypothesis. We introduce MIRA (Medical Image Reflection for Agentic Diagnosis), a medical visual diagnostic framework for autonomous evidence search and reflective verification. MIRA dynamically invokes image-processing operations, including zooming, grounding, pointing, rotation, and measurement, as well as web search, while evaluating the relevance and consistency of the acquired evidence. We develop MIRA through a two-stage training strategy. First, a tool-augmented Monte Carlo Tree Search data engine explores diverse diagnostic hypotheses and jointly verifies visual grounding accuracy and semantic consistency to construct supervised fine-tuning trajectories. Second, reinforcement learning further improves decision-making through online reflective principle evolution: failure cases are distilled into candidate principles, and only principles that improve held-out rollout rewards are retained. Across nine medical visual reasoning benchmarks, MIRA achieves an average score of 64.73, improving its Qwen3-VL-8B backbone by 7.44 points. It also increases useful tool-use judgments from 56.2% to 73.8% and reduces harmful judgments from 8.9% to 1.6%. Qualitative analyses show that MIRA can re-examine evidence, correct premature conclusions, and adapt its tool-use strategy. Project page: https://MIRA-VL.github.io/

AI.tldr: MIRA is a medical visual diagnostic framework that uses reflective verification to autonomously search for evidence—dynamically invoking image-processing and web-search tools while assessing whether tool use is necessary and whether acquired evidence supports the current hypothesis. It is trained via tool-augmented MCTS data generation followed by reinforcement learning with online reflective principle evolution, achieving state-of-the-art results across nine medical visual reasoning benchmarks.
AI.motivation: Medical visual agents that use tools to inspect images and retrieve knowledge can suffer from indiscriminate tool use, which introduces noisy or misleading evidence. Reliable diagnosis requires not only gathering extra observations but also verifying whether tool actions are necessary and whether evidence supports the current hypothesis—capabilities lacking in existing approaches.
AI.method: MIRA uses a two-stage training strategy. First, a tool-augmented Monte Carlo Tree Search data engine explores diverse diagnostic hypotheses and jointly verifies visual grounding accuracy and semantic consistency to build supervised fine-tuning trajectories. Second, reinforcement learning improves decision-making via online reflective principle evolution, where failure cases are distilled into candidate principles and only those that improve held-out rollout rewards are retained.
AI.result: Across nine medical visual reasoning benchmarks, MIRA achieves an average score of 64.73, improving its Qwen3-VL-8B backbone by 7.44 points. It increases useful tool-use judgments from 56.2% to 73.8% and reduces harmful judgments from 8.9% to 1.6%. Qualitative analyses show MIRA can re-examine evidence, correct premature conclusions, and adapt its tool-use strategy.
AI.conclusion: Incorporating reflective verification—evaluating both the necessity of tool actions and the consistency of resulting evidence—substantially improves agentic medical diagnosis, demonstrating the value of rigorous evidence validation over indiscriminate tool use.

title: UniProbe: A Learnable Token-Level Hallucination Detector for Large VLMs using Multi-Structural Internal Representations
summary: Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs) achieve impressive visual reasoning and dialogue capabilities, yet frequently hallucinate content unsupported by the visual input. Effective mitigation requires token-level localization, enabling targeted intervention without discarding the entire response. Existing detectors require expensive full-model fine-tuning, rely on external verifiers that ignore the model's generation process, or reduce internal signals to isolated features and hand-crafted statistics, discarding spatial, sequential, and relational structure. We introduce \textbf{UniProbe}, a lightweight, unified, learnable detector that models a frozen LVLM's heterogeneous computational trace from a single forward pass. UniProbe constructs a directed graph over image patches, query tokens, and generated tokens, with attention weights encoding their relations. It processes this trace with alternating structure-aware modules: a GNN for relational evidence, a ViT for 2-D visual geometry, and a GRU for response order. Interleaving them allows spatial, relational, and sequential evidence to interact throughout the detector. We further develop a streaming variant for hallucination-aware decoding, which detects and resamples hallucinated tokens during generation, and a self-adaptation strategy aligning the detector with the LVLM's own generations. Across diverse LVLM backbones, UniProbe achieves state-of-the-art token-level and object-hallucination detection. During decoding, it reduces object hallucinations by up to 55\% at $1.06\times$ the latency of standard generation.

AI.tldr: UniProbe is a lightweight, unified learnable detector that models a frozen LVLM's heterogeneous computational trace from a single forward pass to achieve state-of-the-art token-level hallucination detection, reducing object hallucinations by up to 55% during decoding at 1.06x latency.
AI.motivation: LVLMs frequently hallucinate content unsupported by visual input. Effective mitigation requires token-level localization for targeted intervention, but existing detectors either require expensive full-model fine-tuning, rely on external verifiers that ignore the generation process, or reduce internal signals to isolated features and hand-crafted statistics, discarding spatial, sequential, and relational structure.
AI.method: UniProbe constructs a directed graph over image patches, query tokens, and generated tokens with attention weights encoding their relations. It processes this trace with alternating structure-aware modules: a GNN for relational evidence, a ViT for 2-D visual geometry, and a GRU for response order, allowing spatial, relational, and sequential evidence to interact. It also includes a streaming variant for hallucination-aware decoding (detecting and resampling hallucinated tokens during generation) and a self-adaptation strategy aligning the detector with the LVLM's own generations.
AI.result: Across diverse LVLM backbones, UniProbe achieves state-of-the-art token-level and object-hallucination detection. During decoding, it reduces object hallucinations by up to 55% at 1.06x the latency of standard generation.
AI.conclusion: UniProbe demonstrates that modeling the full heterogeneous computational trace of a frozen LVLM with interleaved structure-aware modules provides a lightweight and unified solution for hallucination detection and mitigation, achieving superior performance without the need for full-model fine-tuning.

title: PolyLayout: Hierarchical VLM-Guided Layout Generation Beyond Rectangular Rooms
summary: Generating physically plausible 3D room layouts is essential for home furnishing retail, enabling customers to visualize products in their own homes and confidently make purchasing decisions. However, a gap exists between academic research and real-world application: existing solutions primarily focus on algorithmic strategies for furniture placement, largely neglecting the non-rectangular geometries and strict door/window constraints prevalent in real homes. To bridge the gap, we introduce a hybrid, hierarchical framework tailored for retail, specifically designed to support scalable spatial planning applications. Our system decouples generation into three stages: (1) functional furniture clustering and fine-grained intra-zone placement; (2) macro-routing guided by a vision-language model (VLM) to anchor both these clustered zones and any remaining standalone furniture within diverse polygonal boundaries; and (3) rule-based optimization for collision-free micro-arrangements that respect architectural constraints. We evaluate our system on production-scale catalogs and a representative set of irregular real-world topologies. Our results show that our approach attains the highest perceptual plausibility while maintaining good geometric compliance at relatively low latency, and extends to irregular boundaries that existing methods do not natively support.

AI.tldr: The paper presents a hybrid, hierarchical framework for generating physically plausible 3D room layouts tailored to retail applications, handling non-rectangular geometries and door/window constraints that existing academic solutions neglect. The system uses three stages: functional furniture clustering with intra-zone placement, VLM-guided macro-routing within polygonal boundaries, and rule-based optimization for collision-free micro-arrangements.
AI.motivation: There is a gap between academic research on furniture placement and real-world retail needs: existing solutions focus on algorithmic strategies but ignore non-rectangular room geometries and strict door/window constraints common in actual homes, limiting their practical applicability.
AI.method: A three-stage hybrid hierarchical framework: (1) functional furniture clustering and fine-grained intra-zone placement; (2) macro-routing using a vision-language model (VLM) to anchor clustered zones and standalone furniture within diverse polygonal boundaries; (3) rule-based optimization for collision-free micro-arrangements respecting architectural constraints.
AI.result: Evaluated on production-scale catalogs and irregular real-world topologies, the approach achieves the highest perceptual plausibility while maintaining good geometric compliance at relatively low latency, and extends to irregular boundaries not natively supported by existing methods.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework successfully bridges the gap between academic research and retail application by supporting scalable spatial planning in irregular real-world room geometries while maintaining high perceptual quality, geometric compliance, and low latency.

title: The GENEA Challenge 2026: A Large-Scale Disentangled Evaluation of Speech-Driven Gesture Generation on the Seamless Interaction Dataset
summary:
This preprint presents the results of the fourth GENEA Challenge, a large-scale human evaluation of five speech-driven gesture-generation systems trained by participating teams on the Seamless Interaction dataset of dyadic conversations. As in the 2023 GENEA Challenge, we used a disentangled evaluation methodology to assess motion quality and speech alignment without confounding between the two, and performed a dyadic mismatching study to isolate the effect of listening and reacting to the interlocutor. We additionally introduce a new semantic gesture-generation task and a text-mismatching evaluation methodology using the Grounded Gestures subset of the data. In total, we ran four large-scale user studies, collecting over 23,000 votes from 869 test-takers.
  In the motion-realism study, the dataset's filtered segments had substantially higher motion quality than all challenge submissions (68-95% pairwise winrate). In the speech-alignment study, the motion-capture segments provided a conceptual ceiling at 62% alignment score, with the top submission significantly behind at 32% and the rest only slightly above the 0% expected of an input-independent system. In the dyadic study, motion capture again set the ceiling at 65% appropriateness score, but no submission scored substantially above chance, indicating that the systems could not yet respond to the interlocutor. Finally, the semantic mismatching evaluation found highly expressive gestures in the dataset (test-takers identified the matching transcript 79% of the time), yet almost all submissions failed to generate semantically expressive motion, with the best achieving only an 8% appropriateness score.
  The collected votes and outputs will be made publicly available at https://genea-workshop.github.io/2026/challenge/ to facilitate reproducibility and further research.

AI.tldr: This paper reports the fourth GENEA Challenge, evaluating five speech-driven gesture-generation systems via four large-scale user studies (over 23,000 votes from 869 participants). Using disentangled evaluation, dyadic mismatching, and new semantic gesture tasks, results show motion capture consistently outperforms all submissions, with systems failing to match dataset quality in motion realism, speech alignment, dyadic responsiveness, and semantic expressiveness.
AI.motivation: To provide a standardized, large-scale human evaluation of state-of-the-art speech-driven gesture generation systems, extending the GENEA Challenge with new evaluation methodologies including a semantic gesture-generation task and text-mismatching evaluation to address previously under-explored aspects of gesture quality.
AI.method: Four large-scale user studies: (1) motion-realism study, (2) speech-alignment study using disentangled evaluation, (3) dyadic mismatching study isolating interlocutor effects, and (4) a new semantic mismatching evaluation using the Grounded Gestures subset. Five participating teams trained systems on the Seamless Interaction dataset of dyadic conversations.
AI.result: Motion capture data significantly outperforms all submissions (68-95% pairwise winrate in motion realism). Top submission scored 32% vs 62% ceiling in speech alignment. No submission scored above chance in dyadic responsiveness, and the best semantic expressiveness score was only 8% compared to 79% for the dataset.
AI.conclusion: Current gesture-generation systems remain far behind motion capture quality across all evaluated dimensions, particularly failing in dyadic responsiveness and semantic expressiveness. The public release of votes and outputs aims to support reproducibility and further research.

title: Multi-View Relational Distillation for Spatial Reasoning with Vision-Language Models
summary: Vision-language models (VLMs) have achieved strong image and video understanding, yet their visual-spatial representations remain geometrically fragile, leading to failures in spatial reasoning needed for embodied AI, robotics, and autonomous driving. Prior approaches to geometry grounding either fine-tune VLMs on spatial question answering, which can perpetuate spurious visual representations, or fuse features from large geometry-grounded vision models, which substantially increases model size at inference. Knowledge distillation from geometry-grounded vision models offers an alternative, but directly matching multi-view teacher features can disrupt the pretrained alignment between visual and textual representations, degrading object- and language-semantic capabilities. We propose multi-view relational distillation (MVRD), which distills patch-wise cosine similarities across views instead of the teacher features themselves. These relations encode geometric correspondences adequate for spatial understanding, while leaving the student representation underdetermined, allowing it to remain close to its pretrained vision- language space. Across representative VLMs, MVRD improves visual-spatial reasoning, outperforming supervised fine-tuning and feature distillation while approaching feature fusion methods with considerably fewer added parameters and lower latency. We show that MVRD makes visual representations more geometric while retaining language alignment, and generalizes to 3D scene understanding tasks such as object grounding, dense captioning, and question answering.

AI.tldr: MVRD is a multi-view relational distillation method that distills patch-wise cosine similarities across views from geometry-grounded vision models into VLMs, improving spatial reasoning while preserving visual-textual alignment and avoiding large model overhead.
AI.motivation: VLMs have strong image/video understanding but fragile visual-spatial representations, leading to failures in spatial reasoning critical for embodied AI, robotics, and autonomous driving. Existing approaches (fine-tuning on spatial QA, feature fusion) are suboptimal: fine-tuning can perpetuate spurious representations, and feature fusion substantially increases model size. Direct feature distillation can disrupt pretrained visual-textual alignment.
AI.method: MVRD distills patch-wise cosine similarities across multiple views from geometry-grounded teacher vision models, rather than matching teacher features directly. These relational similarities encode geometric correspondences for spatial understanding while leaving the student representation underdetermined, enabling it to stay close to its pretrained vision-language space.
AI.result: MVRD improves visual-spatial reasoning across representative VLMs, outperforming supervised fine-tuning and feature distillation while approaching feature fusion methods with considerably fewer added parameters and lower latency. It also generalizes to 3D scene understanding tasks including object grounding, dense captioning, and question answering.
AI.conclusion: Distilling relational structure (view-wise similarities) rather than teacher features is an effective way to make visual representations more geometric while retaining language alignment, offering a parameter-efficient alternative to feature fusion for spatially-aware VLMs.

title: NullEdit: Stealthy Image Protection via VLM Condition Redirection
summary: Modern image editors combine vision-language models (VLMs) with diffusion transformer backbones to modify a single reference image according to instructions without fine-tuning. This capability also enables unauthorized manipulation of publicly released images.
